mbh.12.103.34.m: People look down even on the gentle, and they shrink from the harsh. Do not be only harsh, do not be only soft: be firm when firmness is needed and gentle when gentleness is.
mbh.12.103.34.sa: मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः / मातीक्ष्णो मा मृदुर्भूस्त्वं तीक्ष्णो भव मृदुर्भव

mbh.12.104.16.m: What was, ceases to be; what was not, comes to be. Grief has no power to change this. Why then should anyone grieve?
roles: Shows the sage wanting the prince to stand on seeing things arise and pass.
mbh.12.104.16.sa: भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति / शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोचेत स कथं नरः

mbh.12.104.28.m: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
roles: Shows enjoying what is present is named as the practice.

mbh.12.104.33.m: Bear the good fortune of others, even though it is not with you. Wise people know how to enjoy good fortune even when it belongs to someone else; good fortune drains away from the one who resents.
roles: Shows the skilled taking joy in good fortune that sits elsewhere.
mbh.12.104.33.sa: सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा / अन्यत्रापि सतीं लक्ष्मीं कुशला भुञ्जते नराः / अभिनिष्यन्दते देही श्रीभूतश्च द्विषज्जनात्

mbh.12.104.57.m: A great lake that has been churned up settles and clears by itself. In the same way a person who has gained wisdom becomes clear by himself.
roles: Shows clarity returning from within when understanding has matured.
mbh.12.104.57.sa: महाह्रदः संक्षुभित आत्मनैव प्रसीदति / `एवं नरः स्वत्मानैव कृतप्रज्ञः प्रसीदति॥'

mbh.12.108.3.m: Honouring one's mother, father and teachers is, I think, the highest duty. One who lives this way wins the worlds and great renown.
roles: Cultivates reverence toward those who raised and taught one.
mbh.12.108.3.sa: मातापित्रोर्गुरूणां च पूजा बहुमता मम / अत्र वर्तन्नरो लोकान्यशश्च महदश्नुते

mbh.12.113.9.m: The cane, seeing the flood coming, bends; no other tree does. And once the force has passed, it stands back up in its place.
roles: Shows resilience as bending and returning to one's place.
mbh.12.113.9.sa: वेतसो वेगमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा नमति नापरे / स च वेगे ह्यतिक्रान्ते स्थानमापद्यते पुनः

scene.s: The Ocean asks the rivers why they uproot great trees but never the reeds. Ganga answers: the reed bends when the flood comes and stands again after; the rigid tree breaks.
scene.t: The river and the reeds

mbh.12.114.15.m: The person who speaks ill of others in front of a crowd only puts his own faults on display, the way a snake raises its hood.
roles: Names the crowd seeing the slanderer.
mbh.12.114.15.sa: परिवादं ब्रुवाणो हि दुरात्मा वै महाजने / प्रकाशयति दोषान्स्वान्सर्पः फणमिवोन्नतम्

mbh.12.114.8.m: Whether such a person praises you or blames you, what difference can it make? It is like a senseless crow cawing in the forest, meaning nothing.
roles: Shows praise and blame from the careless as equally empty.
mbh.12.114.8.sa: प्रकृत्या हि प्रशंसन्वा निन्दन्वा किं करिष्यति / वने काक इवाबुद्धिर्वाश्यमानो निरर्थकम्

mbh.12.138.46.m: A wise enemy is better than a foolish friend.
mbh.12.138.46.sa: श्रेष्ठो हि पण्डितः शत्रुर्न च मित्रमपण्डितः / अमित्रे खलु मार्जारे जीवितं संप्रतिष्ठितम्

scene.s: Caught between a mongoose, an owl and a trapped cat, the mouse Palita makes a deal: he will gnaw the cat free if the cat protects him. Both keep the bargain, then part warily.
scene.t: The cat and the mouse

mbh.12.140.66.m: With gentleness one overcomes the gentle, and with gentleness one overcomes the harsh. Nothing is impossible for gentleness; that is why gentleness is said to be sharper than harshness.
mbh.12.140.66.sa: मृदुनैव मृदुं हन्ति मृदुना हन्ति दारुणम् / नासाध्यं मृदुना किंचित्तस्मात्तीक्ष्णतरो मृदुः

scene.s: A king asks how to deal with rivals. Most of the answer is hard-edged statecraft, but one line holds: gentleness wins over both the gentle and the harsh.
scene.t: Bharadvaja's counsel on gentleness and firmness

mbh.12.144.12.m: Where one's beloved is, even the foot of a tree is home. Without her, even a palace is a wilderness.
roles: Names what a partner's presence is actually worth.
mbh.12.144.12.sa: वृक्षमूलेऽपि दयिता यस्य तिष्ठति तद्गृहम् / प्रासादोपि तया हीनः कान्तार इति निश्चितम्

mbh.12.145.5.m: Hospitality is due even to an enemy who comes to your home. A tree does not withdraw its shade even from the one who comes to cut it down.
roles: Shows care for one who arrives in need, whoever he is.
mbh.12.145.5.sa: अरावप्युचितं कार्यमातिथ्यं गृहमागते / छेत्तुमप्यागते छायां नोपसंहरते द्रुमः

scene.s: A storm-soaked fowler shelters under a tree after trapping a female pigeon. Her mate, grieving, still honours the fowler as a guest, lights a fire for him and, having nothing else, offers himself as food. The shaken fowler gives up hunting.
scene.t: The pigeons and the fowler

mbh.12.17.3.m: Even the one king who rules this whole earth has only one stomach. Why do you praise all this so much?
mbh.12.17.3.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Enough is measured by need, not by reach.
mbh.12.17.3.sa: य इमामखिलां भूमिं शिष्यादेको महीपतिः / तस्याप्युदरमेकं वै किमिदं त्वं प्रशंससि

scene.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
scene.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

mbh.12.17.4.m: You are trying to fill what can never be filled. Not in a day, not in months, not even in a whole lifetime could you fill it.
mbh.12.17.4.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Rest is not on the far side of getting.
mbh.12.17.4.sa: नाह्ना पूरयितुं शक्यां न मासैर्भरतर्षभ / अपूर्यां पूरयन्निच्छामायुषाऽपि न शक्नुयात्

scene.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
scene.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

mbh.12.172.18.m: Where is a good name for the ungrateful, where is a place to stand, where is happiness? No one can trust an ungrateful person.
roles: Shows what is lost when gratitude is lost.
mbh.12.172.18.sa: कुतः कृतघ्नस्य यशः कुतः स्थानं कुतः सुखम् / अश्रद्धेयः कृतघ्नो हि कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः

mbh.12.172.20.m: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
roles: Names gratitude as the disposition to hold.
mbh.12.172.20.sa: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्

mbh.12.172.21.m: Between gaining money and gaining a friend, gaining a friend is better. Money comes easily through friends, and with a friend you can attempt anything.
mbh.12.172.21.sa: अर्थाद्वा मित्रलाभाद्वा मित्रलाभो विशिष्यते / सुलभा मित्रतोऽर्थास्तु मित्रेण यतितुं क्षमम्

mbh.12.173.21.m: From happiness you have fallen into sorrow; you will come to happiness again. No one has sorrow forever, and no one has happiness forever.
roles: Shows footing waiting out the turn.
mbh.12.173.21.sa: सुखात्त्वं दुःखमापन्नः पुनरापत्स्यसे सुखम् / न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्

mbh.12.173.40.m: Idleness feels pleasant but ends in sorrow; capable effort feels hard but gives rise to happiness. Good fortune and prosperity live with the capable, not with the idle.
roles: Shows fortune living with the capable.
mbh.12.173.40.sa: सुखं दुःखान्तमालस्यं दुःखं दाक्ष्यं सुखोदयम् / भूतिश्चैव श्रिया सार्धं दक्षे वसति नालसे

mbh.12.173.41.m: Whether it is happiness or sorrow, something pleasant or unpleasant, meet whatever comes with a heart that is not defeated.
roles: Aparajita hridaya, the undefeated heart, is named.
mbh.12.173.41.sa: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाऽप्रियम् / प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः

mbh.12.173.42.m: Thousands of reasons for grief and hundreds of reasons for fear rush in, day after day, on the unwise person, but not on the wise.
roles: Cultivates discernment as what keeps occasions from entering.
mbh.12.173.42.sa: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च / दिवसेदिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्

mbh.12.173.47.m: Whatever pleasure desire brings in this world, and whatever great happiness there is in heaven, neither is worth a sixteenth part of the happiness that comes when craving ends.
roles: Happiness is relocated from getting to no longer needing.
mbh.12.173.47.sa: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम् / तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशीं कलाम्

mbh.12.173.53.m: Whatever a person begins to think of as 'mine', that very thing becomes a source of anguish when it is lost.
roles: Shows seeing the mechanism of mamatva.
mbh.12.173.53.sa: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम् / तदेव परितापाय नाशे संपद्यते तदा

mbh.12.173.64.m: The one free of expectation sleeps in peace; freedom from expectation is the highest happiness. Turning hope into no-hope, Pingala sleeps peacefully.
roles: Shows ease as a night of sleep.
mbh.12.173.64.sa: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला

scene.s: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
scene.t: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting

mbh.12.174.15.m: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
mbh.12.174.15.sa: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्

scene.s: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
scene.t: Medhavin: the son who woke his father

mbh.12.174.16.m: Who knows whose time of death will come today? Live rightly while you are still young; life is uncertain.
mbh.12.174.16.sa: को हि जानाति कस्याद्य मृत्युकालो भविष्यति / युवैव धर्मशीलः स्यादनित्यं खलु जीवितम् / कृते धर्मे भवेत्कीर्तिरिह प्रेत्य च वै सुखम्

mbh.12.174.20.m: 'This is done, this is still to do, this other thing is half done': while a person is busy like this, attached to his little comforts, death takes him.
roles: A mind that never leaves its tasks.
mbh.12.174.20.sa: इदं कृतमिदं कार्यमिदमन्यत्कृताकृतम् / एवमीहासुखासक्तं कृतान्तः कुरुते वशे

mbh.12.174.35.m: There is no eye like knowledge, no discipline like truth, no sorrow like attachment, and no happiness like letting go.
mbh.12.174.35.sa: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः / नास्ति रागसमंदुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्

mbh.12.174.9.m: The world is struck by death and hemmed in by old age, and the days and nights keep falling like arrows. Why don't you wake up to it?
mbh.12.174.9.sa: मृत्युनाभ्याहतो लोको जरया परिवारितः / अहोरात्राः पतन्त्येते ननु कस्मान्न बुध्यसे / अमोघा रात्रयश्चापि नित्यमायान्ति यान्ति च

mbh.12.175.11.m: Between having nothing and having a kingdom there is this great difference: the rich man is always anxious, as if he were in the jaws of death.
roles: Shows having little recast as freedom.
mbh.12.175.11.sa: आकिञ्चन्ये च राज्ये च विशेषः सुमहानयम् / नित्योद्विग्नो हि धनवान्मृत्योरास्यगतो यथा

mbh.12.175.22.m: Without letting go, no one finds happiness; without letting go, no one reaches the highest; without letting go, no one sleeps free of fear. Let go of everything and be happy.
roles: Names tyaga as the single condition.
mbh.12.175.22.sa: नात्यक्त्वा सुखमाप्नोति नात्यक्त्वा विन्दते परम् / नात्यक्त्वा चाभयः शेते त्यक्त्वा सर्वं सुखी भवेत्

mbh.12.176.25.m: Desire, I know your root: you are born of my own imagining. I will not imagine you any more, and you will be gone, root and all.
mbh.12.176.25.sa: काम जानामि ते मूलं संकल्पात्किल जायसे / न त्वां संकल्पयिष्यामि समूलो नभविष्यसि

mbh.12.176.43.m: I will forgive those who insult me. I will not hurt those who hurt me. When spoken to with hatred, I will reply kindly, paying no attention to the unkindness.
roles: Shows forgiveness taken as a personal vow.
mbh.12.176.43.sa: क्षमिष्ये क्षिपमाणानां न हिंसिष्ये विहिंसितः / द्वेष्यमुक्तः प्रियं वक्ष्याम्यनादृत्य तदप्रियम्

scene.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
scene.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root

mbh.12.176.56.m: My wealth seems endless, because nothing at all is mine. If all of Mithila were burning, nothing of mine would burn.
mbh.12.176.56.sa: अनन्तमिव मे वित्तं यस्य मे नास्ति किंचन / मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किंचन

scene.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
scene.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root

mbh.12.176.63.m: Seeing an osprey with meat in its beak, the birds without meat attack it. By dropping the meat, the osprey is left to live in peace.
roles: Shows peace coming with the dropping.
mbh.12.176.63.sa: सामिषं कुररं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं निरामिषैः / आमिषस्य परित्यागात्कुररः सुखमेधते

mbh.12.176.67.m: A certain arrow-maker was so absorbed in his arrow that he did not even notice the king passing right beside him.
roles: Shows single-pointed attention to the work in hand.
mbh.12.176.67.sa: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिपावासक्तमानसः / समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्

mbh.12.177.24.m: I do not refuse a rightful pleasure that comes to me on its own, nor do I go chasing after one that is hard to get.
roles: Receives what arrives, in keeping with dharma.
mbh.12.177.24.sa: न सन्निपतितं धर्म्यमुपभोगं यदृच्छया / प्रत्याचक्षे न चाप्येनमनुरुध्ये सुदुर्लभम्

scene.s: Prahlada meets a sage who lives like a python, taking what comes and not chasing. The sage explains how ceasing to chase made him content.
scene.t: The python-sage (Ajagara vrata)

mbh.12.178.12.m: We long for hands the way you long for money. There is no gain greater than having hands.
roles: Names hands and their works as first wealth.
mbh.12.178.12.sa: पाणिमद्भ्यः स्पृहाऽस्माकं यथा तव धनस्य वै / न पाणिलाभादधिको लाभः कश्चन विद्यते

scene.s: A young brahmin, Kashyapa, knocked down by a rich man's chariot, wants to die in humiliation. A jackal tells him how lucky he is to have hands and a human life, and that craving grows like fire fed with wood. The jackal is Indra.
scene.t: Kashyapa and the jackal: the gift of hands

mbh.12.178.26.m: There is no satisfaction in getting what you want. Craving is not put out by water; it only blazes up more, like a fire fed with fuel.
roles: Shows the want that grows each time it is fed.
mbh.12.178.26.sa: न तृप्तिः प्रियलाभेऽस्ति तृष्णा नाद्भिः प्रशाम्यति / संप्रज्वलति सा भूयः समिद्भिरिव पावकः

mbh.12.210.16.m: I have taken refuge in the Lord, protector of the world, thousand-eyed, wondrous, the highest abode, master of past, future and present.
mbh.12.210.16.sa: लोकनाथं सहस्राक्षमद्भुतं परदं पदम् / भगवन्तं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुम्

mbh.12.230.31.m: It does not suit your reputation or your family that you, who have everything, should wish to boast over me, who have lost it.
roles: Names the gloating as unworthy without begging or raging.
mbh.12.230.31.sa: न त्वेतदनुरूपं ते यशसो वा कुलस्य च / समृद्धार्थोऽसमृद्धार्थं यन्मां कत्थितुमिच्छसि

mbh.12.231.41.m: This is not a time for putting forth strength; a time for calm has come. Time sets everything in place, and time ripens everything.
mbh.12.231.41.sa: न तु विक्रमकालोऽयं शान्तिकालोऽयमागतः / कालः स्थापयते सर्वं कालः पचति वै तथा

scene.s: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his defeated rival Bali living as a donkey in an empty house and mocks him. Bali calmly answers that fortune has lived with a thousand Indras before, that time gives and takes, and that this is a season for calm.
scene.t: Bali and Indra: the fortune that moves on

mbh.12.231.62.m: This royal fortune that you think rests with you: that is false. It has never stayed with anyone. It lived with thousands of Indras greater than you, and has now left me and come to you.
roles: Shows rise and fall belong to fortune's movement.
mbh.12.231.62.sa: यामेतां प्राप्य जानीषे राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम् / स्थिता मयीति तन्मिथ्या नैषा ह्येकत्र तिष्ठति स्थिता हीन्द्रसहस्रेषु त्वद्विशिष्टतमेष्वियम् / मां च लोला परित्यज्य त्वामगाद्विबुधाधिप

mbh.12.25.31.m: Happiness and sorrow, rise and fall, gain and loss, death and life: everyone receives all of these in turn. So do not be thrown off by them, and do not get carried away either.
mbh.12.25.31.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Neither crushed nor carried away is the instruction.
mbh.12.25.31.sa: सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च / लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च / पर्यायतः सर्वमवाप्तुवन्ति / तस्मान्न मुह्येन्न च संप्रहृष्येत्

mbh.12.26.29.m: For every living being, meeting and parting are certain. Like bubbles on water, they appear and are gone.
mbh.12.26.29.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.26.29.sa: संयोगा विप्रयोगाश्च जातानां प्राणिनां ध्रुवम् / बुद्धुदा इव तोयेषु भवन्ति न भवन्ति च

mbh.12.268.9.m: Jajali, the one who is always a friend to all, devoted to the good of all, in action, thought and word, is the one who truly knows dharma.
mbh.12.268.9.sa: सर्वेषां यः सुहृन्नित्यं सर्वेषां च हिते रतः / कर्मणा मनसा वाचा स धर्मं वेद जाजले

mbh.12.27.12.m: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
mbh.12.27.12.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Shows asking which of the two this is.
mbh.12.27.12.sa: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते

mbh.12.27.40.m: 'Where was I before? Where will I go? Who am I, really, and why am I here? Why should I grieve, and for what?' Ask these, and steady the mind.
mbh.12.27.40.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.27.40.sa: क्वासे क्व च गमिष्यामि कोऽन्वहं किमिहास्थितः / कस्मात्किमनुशोचेयमित्येवं स्थापयेन्मनः

mbh.12.27.49.m: Days do not come back, nor months, nor years. And beings, once parted, do not meet again in the same way.
mbh.12.27.49.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Shows meetings are understood as temporary by nature.
mbh.12.27.49.sa: न ह्यहानि निवर्तन्ते न मासा न पुनः समाः / जातानां सर्वभूतानां न पुनर्वै समागमः

mbh.12.27.52.m: No one ever gets to live together with anyone forever, not even with one's own body, let alone with anyone else.
mbh.12.27.52.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.27.52.sa: नायमत्यन्तसंवासो लभ्यते जातु केनचित् / अपि स्वेन शरीरेण किमुतान्येन केनचित्

mbh.12.272.23.m: A grown person is freed from his bonds as fruit drops from the tree. But a father, even suffering through his love, never lets go of his child.
roles: Shows what a father carries for a child.
mbh.12.272.23.sa: मुच्यते बन्धनात्पुरुषं फलं वृक्षान्प्रमुच्यते / क्लिश्यन्नपि सुतस्नेहैः पिता पुत्रं न मुञ्चति

mbh.12.272.28.m: Even with sons and grandsons around him, someone who still has his mother to turn to lives like a two-year-old, even at a hundred.
roles: Names a living mother as a shelter one still has.
mbh.12.272.28.sa: पुत्रपौत्रोपपन्नोपि जननीं यः समाश्रितः / अपि वर्षशतस्यान्ते स द्विहायनवच्चरेत्

mbh.12.272.29.m: Capable or not, thin or well-fed, a mother protects her child. No one else nurtures like that.
roles: Shows care not depending on the child's success.
mbh.12.272.29.sa: समर्थं वाऽसमर्थं वा कृशं वाप्यकृशं तथा / रक्षत्येव सुतं माता नान्यः पोष्टा विधानतः

mbh.12.272.30.m: Only then does a person become old, only then truly sorrowful, only then does the world feel empty: when he is parted from his mother.
roles: Says exactly what losing a mother does: one is suddenly old and the world is empty.
mbh.12.272.30.sa: तदा स वृद्धो भवति तदा भवति दुःखितः / तदा शून्यं जगत्तस्य यदा मात्रा वियुज्यते

mbh.12.272.31.m: There is no shade like a mother, no refuge like a mother, no protection like a mother, no one as dear as a mother.
roles: Names a mother as shade, refuge, protection.
mbh.12.272.31.sa: नास्ति मातृसमा च्छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः / नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया

mbh.12.272.51.m: They say ruin is born of jealousy; even ascetics fall to it. Jealousy threw me into a sea of wrongdoing.
mbh.12.272.51.sa: ईर्ष्याजं व्यसनं प्राहुस्तेन चैवोर्ध्वरेतसः / ईर्ष्यया त्वहमाक्षिप्तो मग्नो दुष्कृतसागरे

mbh.12.272.69.m: Make a friend slowly, and give one up slowly. A friendship made slowly is one that lasts long.
roles: Shows slow friendship is the lasting kind.
mbh.12.272.69.sa: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति

mbh.12.272.73.m: So, in every matter, a person should think it over and decide slowly; then he does not suffer regret for long.
mbh.12.272.73.sa: एवं सर्वेषु कार्येषु विमृश्य पुरुषस्ततः / चिरेण निश्चयं कृत्वा चिरं न परितप्यते

mbh.12.28.14.m: Srinjaya, you, I and all creatures will die without being freed from joy and sorrow. So why such lament?
mbh.12.28.14.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Names that no one is exempt.
mbh.12.28.14.sa: सुखदुःखैरहं त्वं च प्रजाः सर्वाश्च सृञ्जय / अविमुक्ता मरिष्यामस्तत्र का परिदेवना

scene.s: Krishna tells Yudhishthira how Narada consoled King Srinjaya, whose son had died, by recounting sixteen legendary kings far greater than his son who also died. Moved, Srinjaya listens, and Narada restores the boy.
scene.t: The sixteen kings: Narada consoles Srinjaya

mbh.12.305.14.m: The rush of speech, the surge of anger, the itch to scheme, the urges of belly and body: the one who can withstand these urges when they rise, him I call a true sage.
mbh.12.305.14.sa: वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं / विधित्सावेगमुदरोपस्थवेगम् / एतान्वेगान्यो विषहेदुदीर्णां / स्तं मन्येऽहं ब्राह्मणं वै मुनिं च

mbh.12.305.15.m: One who does not get angry is better than those who do; the patient are better than the impatient; the humane better than the inhuman; the knowing better than the ignorant.
mbh.12.305.15.sa: अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्ट / स्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः / अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्ट / स्तथाऽज्ञानाज्ज्ञानवान्वै विशिष्टः

mbh.12.305.23.m: Fault-finders are never as eager to speak of a person's good qualities as they are to speak of his flaws.
roles: Shows criticism weighed for its source.
mbh.12.305.23.sa: न तथा वक्तुमिच्छन्ति कल्याणान्पुरुषे गुणान् / यथैषां वक्तुमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यमनुयुञ्जकाः

mbh.12.305.27.m: Whatever an angry person offers, gives, endures in discipline or sacrifices, Yama takes it all away. The angry man's labour is wasted.
roles: Shows anger cancelling one's own good work.
mbh.12.305.27.sa: यत्क्रोधनो यजति यद्ददाति / यद्वा तपस्तप्यति यज्जुहोति / वैवस्वतस्तद्धरतेऽस्य सर्वं / मोघः श्रमो भवति हि क्रोधनस्य

mbh.12.305.32.m: The people one argues with, the people one keeps company with, and what one wishes to become: that is what a person becomes. Whether he serves the good or the bad, the disciplined or a thief, just as a cloth takes on the colour of its dye, he falls under their influence.
roles: What one wishes to become is counted among the shaping forces.
mbh.12.305.32.sa: यादृशैः संविवदते यादृशांश्चोपसेवते / यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः यदि सन्तं सेवति यद्यसन्तं / तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव / वासो यथा रागवशं प्रयाति / तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति

mbh.12.305.38.m: Silence, they say, is better than speech. To speak the truth is the second. To speak what is right is the third. To speak what is kind as well is the fourth and best.
roles: Cultivates kindness as the finishing quality of true speech.
mbh.12.305.38.sa: अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः / सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् / धर्म्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं / प्रियं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम्

mbh.12.305.8.m: Do not wound others where it hurts, do not speak cruelly, do not take from those who have less. Never say words that make another person flinch; such words are scorching and lead to dark places.
roles: Shows one feeling the other's flinch before speaking.
mbh.12.305.8.sa: नारुतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी / न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत / ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत / न तां वदेदुशतिं पापलोक्याम्

mbh.12.305.9.m: Arrows of words fly from the mouth, and the one they strike grieves day and night. They land on nothing but the tender spots of another; so a wise person never lets them fly at others.
roles: Sees speech from the receiver's side.
mbh.12.305.9.sa: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्यतन्ति / यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि / परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति / तान्पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु

mbh.12.337.11.m: Always guard your discipline from anger and your good fortune from envy; guard your learning from both pride and insult, and guard yourself from carelessness.
roles: Shows four things protected from their own enemies.
mbh.12.337.11.sa: नित्यं क्रोधात्तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेच्च मत्सरात् / विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः

mbh.12.337.13.m: Speaking the truth is good, but better than mere truth is to speak what helps. What is truly for the good of all beings, that is what I hold to be truth.
roles: Shows truth is measured by the welfare of beings.
mbh.12.337.13.sa: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यादपि हितं वदेत् / यद्भूतहितमत्यन्तमेतत्सत्यं मतं मम

mbh.12.338.12.m: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
roles: Shows withholding attention from the loop as the practice.
mbh.12.338.12.sa: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्

mbh.12.338.13.m: Heal the pain of the mind with wisdom and the pain of the body with medicine. That is what knowledge can do; don't behave like a child about it.
mbh.12.338.13.sa: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः / एतद्विज्ञानमसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्

mbh.12.338.15.m: No one should sit alone grieving over a trouble that has struck everyone. Instead of grieving, act to remedy it if you see a way.
roles: Shows acting where a way appears.
mbh.12.338.15.sa: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति / अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम्

mbh.12.338.19.m: Reaching one level of wealth after another, people remain unsatisfied and come to ruin. The wise come to contentment.
mbh.12.338.19.sa: अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिकीं नराः / अतृप्ता यान्ति विध्वंसं संतोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः

mbh.12.338.21.m: There is no end to thirst; contentment is the highest happiness. That is why the wise see contentment itself as wealth.
roles: Names contentment as the real wealth.
mbh.12.338.21.sa: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् / तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः

mbh.12.338.22.m: Not even for the blink of an eye does life stand still. In a body that is passing, why brood as if things last forever?
roles: Impermanence seen in one's own body.
mbh.12.338.22.sa: निमेषमात्रमपि हि वयो गच्छन्न तिष्ठति / स्वशरीरेष्वनित्येषु नित्यं किमनुचिन्तयेत्

mbh.12.338.9.m: Whoever keeps grieving over the past, over what has died or been lost, gets sorrow on top of sorrow: two misfortunes instead of one.
roles: Shows the loop as a second misfortune one can decline.
mbh.12.338.9.sa: मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योऽतीतमनुशोचति / दुःखेन लभते दुःखं द्वावनर्थौ प्रपद्यते

mbh.12.46.122.m: Those who bow to Govinda, the unfailing one, dark like the flax flower and dressed in yellow, have no fear.
mbh.12.46.122.sa: अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्युतम् / ये नमस्यन्ति गोविन्दं न तेषां विद्यते भयम्

mbh.12.46.125.m: Salutations to Vishnu, who draws a protective circle against the terror of hell, the log to cling to in the whirlpools of the river of worldly life.
roles: Clings to God as to a log.

mbh.12.46.127.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.

mbh.12.46.131.m: For the devotee who has taken refuge in you and longs to reach the goal he wants, think, lotus-eyed one, best of gods, of whatever is truly good for him.
mbh.12.46.131.sa: त्वां प्रपन्नाय भक्ताय गतिमिष्टां जिगीषवे / यच्छ्रेयः पुण्डरीकाक्ष तद्ध्यायस्व सुरोत्तम

scene.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
scene.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

mbh.12.46.14.m: Bhishma, tiger among men, lying on the bed of arrows, pure, with folded hands, fixed his thoughts on Krishna in deed, mind and word.
mbh.12.46.14.sa: भीष्मस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / शरतल्पगतः कृष्णं प्रदध्यौ प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः

scene.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
scene.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

mbh.12.51.11.m: I cannot make out the directions, nor the sky, nor the earth. I stand only by your strength, Madhusudana.
mbh.12.51.11.sa: न दिशः संप्रजानामि नाकाशं न च मेदिनीम् / केवलं तव वीर्येण तिष्ठामि मधुसूदन

scene.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
scene.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

mbh.12.53.17.m: The burning, the confusion, the exhaustion, the weariness, the weakness and the pain — by your grace, Varshneya, they left me at once.
mbh.12.53.17.sa: दाहो मोहः श्रमश्चैव क्लमो ग्लानिस्तथा रुजा / तव प्रसादाद्वार्ष्णेय सद्यो व्यपगतानि मे

scene.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
scene.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

mbh.12.53.23.m: I feel as if I have become young again, strengthened by meditating on you. By your grace, Janardana, I am able to speak what is good.
mbh.12.53.23.sa: युवेवास्मि समावृत्तस्त्वदनुध्यानबृंहितः / वक्तुं श्रेयः समर्थोऽस्मि त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन

scene.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
scene.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

mbh.12.55.16.m: If an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself over it. Keep applying yourself again and again; this is the highest rule for those who lead.
mbh.12.55.16.sa: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः

mbh.12.7.13.m: Fathers long for every good thing for their children, and strive for them with discipline, prayer and patience. Mothers, through fasts and vows, conceive them and carry them for ten months.
mbh.12.7.13.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
roles: Shows listing what parents did before one could know it.
mbh.12.7.13.sa: बहुकल्याणमिच्छन्त ईहन्ते पितरः सुतान् / तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण वन्दनेन तितिक्षया उपवासैस्तथेज्याभिर्व्रतकौतुकमङ्गलैः / लभन्ते मातरो गर्भांस्तान्मासान्दश बिभ्रति

scene.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
scene.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

mbh.12.7.34.m: Arjuna, a wrong that has been done can be undone by doing good: by admitting it openly, by remorse, by giving, by discipline.
mbh.12.7.34.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.7.34.sa: धनञ्जय कृतं पापं कल्याणेनोपहन्यते / [ख्यापनेनानुतापेन दानेन तपसाऽपि वा / निवृत्त्या तीर्थगमनाच्छुतिस्मृतिजपेन वा॥]

scene.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
scene.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

mbh.12.80.17.m: The one who doesn't burn with resentment at your rise and grows sad at your decline: that, they say, is the mark of the best friend.
roles: Shows the friend one can try to be.
mbh.12.80.17.sa: यस्तु वृद्ध्या न तप्येत क्षये दीनतरो भवेत् / एतदुत्तममित्रस्य निमित्तमभिचक्षते

mbh.12.80.36.m: When others wrong you, your own people are your refuge. No one else will stand up against your humiliation the way family does.
mbh.12.80.36.sa: निकृतस्य नरैरन्यैर्ज्ञातिरेव परायणम् / नान्यो निकारं सहते ज्ञातिर्ज्ञातेः कदाचन

mbh.12.81.11.m: I am like the mother of two gamblers playing against each other, great sage. I cannot wish one victory without wishing the other defeat.
roles: Shows Krishna torn between two sides of his own family.
mbh.12.81.11.sa: सोऽहं कित्नवमातेव द्वयोरपि महामुने / नैकस्य जयमाशंसे द्वितीयस्य पराजयम्

mbh.12.81.21.m: Giving food and help as far as you can, patience, sincerity, gentleness, and honouring each person as they deserve: this is the weapon not made of iron.
roles: Shows titiksha toward one's own people.
mbh.12.81.21.sa: शक्त्याऽन्नदानं सततं तितिक्षाऽऽर्जवमार्दवम् / यथार्हप्रतिपूजा च शस्त्रमेतदनायसम्

scene.s: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
scene.t: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron

mbh.12.81.22.m: When relatives are about to say bitter or petty things, calm their hearts, their words and their minds with your own words.
roles: Shows answering bitterness with calming speech.
mbh.12.81.22.sa: ज्ञातीनां वक्तुकामानां कटुकानि लधूनि च / गिरा त्वं हृदयं वाचं शमयस्य मनांसि च

scene.s: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
scene.t: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron

mbh.12.81.6.m: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.
roles: Shows Krishna says plainly that his relatives' words burn him daily.
mbh.12.81.6.sa: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मथ्नाति दहृयं मम / वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मां दहति नित्यदा

mbh.12.84.5.m: The person who never says a word and always wears a frown is disliked by everyone, for he does not practise kind speech. But the one who notices everyone, speaks to them first, and greets them with a smile, wins the whole world's goodwill.
roles: Shows warm speech as a daily practice.
mbh.12.84.5.sa: यो हि नाभाषते किंचित्सर्वदा भुकुटीमुखः / द्वेष्यो भवति भूतानां स सान्त्वमिह नाचरन् यस्तु सर्वमभिप्रेक्ष्य पूर्वमेवाभिभाषते / स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च तस्य लोकः प्रसीदति

mbh.12.84.7.m: Even a gift, if it is given without kind words, does not please anyone, like food without any seasoning.
roles: Shows kind words make giving land.
mbh.12.84.7.sa: दानमेव हि सर्वत्र सान्त्वेनानभिजल्पितम् / न प्रीणयति भूतानि निर्व्यञ्जनमिवाशनम्

mbh.13.10.25.m: As a person ages, his hair grows old, his teeth grow old, his eyes and ears grow old. Only craving does not grow old.
roles: Shows wanting as the one thing in us that never tires.
mbh.13.10.25.sa: जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः / चक्षुः श्रोत्रे च जीर्येते तृष्णैका न तु जीर्यते

mbh.13.11.26.m: You should not ask me to abandon this tree after so long. I lived off it when it flourished; how can I leave it now that it is in trouble?
roles: Holds to the bond through its hard season.
mbh.13.11.26.sa: नार्हसे मां सहस्राक्ष द्रुमं त्याजयितुं चिरात् / समस्थमुपजीवन्वै विषमस्थं कथं त्यजेत्

mbh.13.161.111.m: Never speak ill of others or say unpleasant things. A person who wants to prosper should never stir up anyone's anger.
roles: Shows speech that does not wound or provoke.
mbh.13.161.111.sa: परापवादं न ब्रूयान्नाप्रियं च कदाचन / न मन्युः कश्चिदुत्पाद्यः पुरुषेणि भवार्थिना

mbh.13.161.119.m: An aged relative, a friend, a sister with no one to support her, a teacher, a person of good family or learning who has fallen poor: protect them as you are able, and give them a place in your home.
mbh.13.161.119.sa: वृद्धो ज्ञातिस्तथा मित्रमनाथा च स्वसा गुरुः / कुलीनः पण्डित इति रक्ष्या निःस्वः स्वशक्तितः / गृहे वासयितव्यास्ते धन्यमायुष्यमेव च

mbh.13.161.14.m: One who is slow to anger, truthful, harms no living being, does not envy and is not crooked lives a hundred years.
roles: Shows harmlessness and freedom from envy.
mbh.13.161.14.sa: अक्रोधनः सत्यवादी भूतानामविहिंसकः / अनसूयुरजिह्मश्च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति

mbh.13.161.35.m: Barbed arrows and spears can be pulled out of the body, but the dart of a cruel word cannot be removed. It stays lodged in the heart.
roles: Shows what a sentence does for the speaker.
mbh.13.161.35.sa: कर्णिनालीकनाराचान्निर्हरन्ति शरीरतः / वाक्शल्यस्तु न निर्हर्तुं शक्यो हृदिशयो हि सः

mbh.13.161.36.m: Never taunt anyone for a missing limb or an extra one, for lack of learning, for age, for lack of looks or money, or for lack of standing.
roles: Shows no one is to be mocked for what they lack.

mbh.13.161.45.m: Don't sleep past sunrise. On rising, first greet your mother and father, and your teacher or another elder; that is how a long life is won.
roles: Shows a daily act of respect to parents.
mbh.13.161.45.sa: न चाभ्युदितसायी स्यात्प्रायश्चित्ती तथा भवेत् / मातापितरमुत्थाय पूर्वमेवाभिवादयेत् / आचार्यमथवाऽप्यन्तं तथाऽऽयुर्विदन्ते महत्

mbh.13.162.12.m: If undivided brothers decide to split the property while the father lives, the father should never give unequal shares.
roles: Shows a child given less the unequal share was wrong.
mbh.13.162.12.sa: भ्रातॄणामविभक्तानामुत्थानमपि चेत्सह / न पुत्रभागं विषमं पिता दद्यात्कदाचन

mbh.13.162.15.m: A teacher outweighs ten instructors, a father ten teachers, and a mother ten fathers, even the whole earth. There is no teacher equal to a mother.
roles: Shows placing the mother above every other teacher.
mbh.13.162.15.sa: दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान्पिता दश / दश चैव पितॄन्माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि / गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः

mbh.13.162.4.m: At times the elder should act blind, or slow, even though he is wise. If a younger one goes wrong, point it out indirectly.
mbh.13.162.4.sa: अन्धः स्यादन्धवेलायां जडः स्यादपि वा बुधः / परिहारेण तद्ब्रूयाद्यस्तेषां स्याद्व्यतिक्रमः

mbh.13.162.5.m: Outsiders who burn at a family's good fortune try to break it apart, sowing division between brothers. Those who stay close are not divided.
roles: Watchfulness about who profits from a family split.
mbh.13.162.5.sa: प्रत्यक्षं भिन्नहृदया भेदयेयुर्यथाऽहिताः / `श्रियाऽभितप्तास्तद्भेदान्नभिन्नाः स्युः समाहिताः' / श्रियाऽभितप्ताः कौन्तेय भेदकामास्तथाऽरयः

mbh.13.162.6.m: The eldest can make a family flourish, or destroy it. Usually, when he ruins everything, it is through arrogance.
roles: Names arrogance in the leader as the family-breaker.
mbh.13.162.6.sa: ज्येष्ठः कुलं वर्धयति विनाशयति वा पुनः / हन्ति सर्वमपि ज्येष्ठः प्रायो दुर्विनयादिह

mbh.13.175.8.m: Do not do to another what you would find hurtful yourself. This, in short, is dharma; anything else comes from desire.
roles: Uses one's own pain as the measure of another's.
mbh.13.175.8.sa: न तत्परस्य संदध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः / एष साङ्ग्राहिको धर्मः कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते

mbh.13.254.145.m: Lotus-eyed one with wide eyes, lotus-naveled, best of gods, Janardana, be the protector of the devotees who love you.
roles: Shows a short prayer for protection.
mbh.13.254.145.sa: पद्मपत्रविशालक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम / भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन

mbh.13.273.39.m: Protect always, lotus-eyed Purushottama, your devotee, whose goal you are, calm, generous, owning nothing. Give me leave, Krishna, Vaikuntha, Purushottama.
mbh.13.273.39.sa: त्वद्भक्तं त्वद्गतिं शान्तमुदारमपरिग्रहम् / त्रायस्व पुण्डरीकाक्ष पुरुषोत्तम नित्यशः / अनुजानीहि मां कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम

scene.s: When the sun turns north, Bhishma, after fifty-eight nights on the arrows, takes leave of the family, asks Krishna to protect him and to give him leave to go. Krishna says there is no fault in him and lets him go; Bhishma's last words to the family are to hold to truth and kindness.
scene.t: Bhishma asks Krishna's leave to die

mbh.13.43.45.m: For those sunk in the mire of great delusion and the chase for wealth, Hari is the way; the single-minded, intent on meditation, come to me through renunciation.
mbh.13.43.45.sa: महामोहार्थपङ्के तु निमग्रानां गतिर्हरिः / एकान्तिनो ध्यानपरा यतिभावाद्ब्रजन्ति माम्

mbh.13.9.9.m: Just as seed sown without a field bears no fruit, so destiny does not succeed without human effort. Effort is the field and destiny the seed; only when field and seed come together does the harvest flourish.
roles: Effort is the field in which anything can grow.
mbh.13.9.9.sa: यथा बीजं विना क्षेत्रमुप्तं भवति निष्फलम् / तथा पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति क्षेत्रं पुरुषकारस्तु दैवं बीजमुदाहृतम् / क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात्ततः सस्यं समृद्ध्यते

mbh.14.12.15.m: Now a battle is upon you where arrows are useless, and servants and relatives too: one you must fight alone, with your own self.
roles: Calls for taking up the inner fight.
mbh.14.12.15.sa: यत्र नैव शरैः कार्यं न भृत्यैर्न च बन्धुभिः / आत्मनैकेन योद्धव्यं तत्ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्

scene.s: As Yudhishthira still grieves, Krishna tells him his real battle has begun: one fought alone, with his own mind, where 'mine' is death and 'not mine' is freedom.
scene.t: Krishna on the war within

mbh.14.13.13.m: Whoever tries to kill me, relying on the strength of some weapon, finds me reborn in that very weapon.
roles: Shows the means of fighting desire becoming its new seat.
mbh.14.13.13.sa: यो मां प्रयतते हन्तुं ज्ञात्वा प्रहरणे बलम् / तस्य तस्मिन्प्रहरणे पुनः प्रादुर्भवाम्यहम्
mbh.14.13.13.sp: Desire (the Kama Gita, quoted by Krishna)

mbh.14.13.3.m: Two syllables are death; three syllables are the eternal. 'Mama' (mine) in two syllables is death; 'na mama' (not mine) is the eternal.
roles: Shows 'Not mine' identified with the eternal.
mbh.14.13.3.sa: द्व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् / ममेति द्व्यक्षरो मृत्युर्नममेति च शाश्वतम्

mbh.14.13.6.m: Even if someone gains the whole earth with everything on it, what harm can it do him if he has no sense of 'mine'? But one living in the forest on wild food, if he clings to his possessions, is already in death's jaws.
roles: Lets go inwardly while keeping one's place in life.
mbh.14.13.6.sa: लब्ध्वा हि पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां सहस्थावरजङ्गमाम् / ममत्वं यस्य नैव स्यात्किं तया स करिष्यति अथवा वसतः पार्थ वने वन्येन जीवतः / ममता यस्य वित्तेषु मृत्योरांस्ये स वर्तते

mbh.14.32.12.m: So, seeing greed clearly for what it is, restrain it with steadiness and seek to rule within yourself. That is the true kingdom, there is no other; the self, rightly understood, is the king.
roles: Names the self rightly known as the king.
mbh.14.32.12.sa: तस्मादेतं सम्यगवेक्ष्य लोभं / निगृह्य धृत्याऽऽत्मनि राज्यमिच्छेत् / एतद्राज्यं नान्यदस्तीह राज्य- / मात्मैव राजा विदितो यथावत्

mbh.14.52.7.m: With you as our protector, Madhusudana, we Pandavas crossed the Kuru ocean, using you as our raft. (Protect us, your devotees who rely on you, here and hereafter.)
roles: Shows looking back and naming who carried one through.
mbh.14.52.7.sa: नाथवन्तश्च भवता पाण्डवा मधुसूदन / भवन्तं प्लवमासाद्य तीर्णाः स्म कुरुसागरम् / `भक्तांस्त्वमाश्रितानस्मान्पालयामुत्र चेह च।'

scene.s: After the war and the Anugita, Arjuna thanks Krishna as they ride to Hastinapura.

mbh.14.53.15.m: I made every effort earlier to bring the Kauravas to peace. But they could not be brought to agree, however I tried.
roles: Shows standing by an honest effort.
mbh.14.53.15.sa: कृतो यत्नो मया पूर्वं सौशाम्ये कौरवान्प्रति / नाशक्यन्त यदा साम्ये ते स्थापयितुमञ्जसा

scene.s: Returning home after the war, Krishna meets the sage Uttanka, who is furious that Krishna let the cousins destroy each other and threatens to curse him. Krishna explains that he tried hard for peace and was refused, and calms him.
scene.t: Uttanka confronts Krishna

mbh.14.66.15.m: Vasudeva, mighty-armed, through you Devaki is blessed in her son. You are our way and our ground; this family depends on you.
mbh.14.66.15.sa: वासुदेव महाबाहो सुप्रजा देवकी त्वया / त्वं नो गतिः प्रतिष्ठा च त्वदायत्तमिदं कुलम्

scene.s: Abhimanyu's son is born dead, struck in the womb by Ashvatthama's weapon. Kunti, Subhadra and Uttara beg Krishna for help, reminding him of his promise. Krishna, on the strength of his own truthfulness, revives the child, who is named Parikshit.
scene.t: The stillborn heir and Krishna's promise

mbh.14.92.69.m: Hunger drives out wisdom and pushes aside the sense of right; one overcome by hunger loses even his steadiness.
roles: Names understanding for those acting from need.
mbh.14.92.69.sa: क्षुधा निर्णुदति प्रज्ञां धर्मबुद्धिं व्यपोहति / क्षुधापरिगतज्ञानो धृतिं त्यजति चैव ह

mbh.14.92.75.m: One who has a thousand and gives a hundred, one who has a hundred and gives ten, and one who has nothing and gives a little water, each according to his means: all earn equal merit.
roles: Shows having enough to give from.
mbh.14.92.75.sa: सहस्रशक्तिश्च शतं शतशक्तिर्दशापि च / दद्यादपश्च यः शक्त्या सर्वे तुल्यफलाः स्मृताः

mbh.14.92.77.m: Dharma is not pleased by lavish gifts so much as by small ones, honestly earned and given with sincerity.
roles: Shows what is honestly one's own is enough to give.
mbh.14.92.77.sa: न धर्मः प्रीयते तात दानैर्दत्तैर्महाफलैः / न्यायलब्धैर्यथा सूक्ष्मैः श्रुद्धापूतैः स तुष्यति

mbh.3.12.134.m: The sky may fall, the Himalaya may split, the earth may shatter into pieces, the ocean may dry up, Krishna, but my word will not prove false.
roles: Shows a promise that will be kept.
mbh.3.12.134.sa: पतेद्द्यौर्हिमवाञ्शीर्येत्पृथिवी शकली भवेत् / शुष्येत्तोयनिधिः कृष्णे न मे मोघं वचो भवेत्

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi weeps to Krishna about her humiliation in the dice hall; he answers with a vow.

mbh.3.12.46.m: You are mine alone, and I am yours; those who are mine are yours. Whoever hates you hates me; whoever follows you follows me.
roles: Shows God taking the devotee's side as his own.
mbh.3.12.46.sa: ममैव त्वं तवैवाहं ये मदीयास्तवैव ते / यस्त्वां द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्त्वामनु स मामनु

scene.s: Krishna visits the exiled Pandavas in the Kamyaka forest and tells Arjuna 'you are mine and I am yours'. Draupadi then comes to him 'seeking refuge with the refuge', tells him, out of closeness, everything done to her in the dice-hall and since, and weeps that she has no one, not even him. Krishna promises she will see justice.
scene.t: Draupadi tells Krishna her sorrow

mbh.3.133.13.m: When deciding between right and wrong, weigh what is heavier against what is lighter, and choose the course where the greater good lies.
mbh.3.133.13.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Shibi and the dove
mbh.3.133.13.sa: गुरुलाघवमाज्ञाय धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये / यतो भूयांस्ततो राजन्कुरु धर्मविनिश्चयम्

scene.s: A frightened dove flies to King Shibi for refuge; a hawk demands it back as its rightful food. Shibi offers the hawk anything else, finally his own flesh weighed against the dove, and climbs onto the scale himself. The birds reveal themselves as gods.
scene.t: King Shibi and the dove

mbh.3.135.10.m: Growth isn't measured by the size of the body. A short tree that bears fruit has grown; a tall one that bears none has not.
roles: Shows standing on what one can actually do.
mbh.3.135.10.sa: न ज्ञायते कायवृद्ध्या विवृद्धि- / र्यथाऽष्ठीला शाल्मलेः संप्रवृद्धाः / ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो / यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः

mbh.3.135.12.m: A person is not old because his head is grey. The one who truly understands, even if young, is the one the gods call an elder.
roles: Ashtavakra holds his ground without insult and asks to be judged on knowledge.
mbh.3.135.12.sa: न तेन स्थविरो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः / बालोपि यः प्रजानाति तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः

mbh.3.152.27.m: Without learning what is right and sitting with those who have lived longer, no one can know it, not even someone as wise as Brihaspati.
mbh.3.152.27.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Bhima and Hanuman
mbh.3.152.27.sa: न हि धर्ममविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च / धर्मो वै वेदितुं शक्यो बृहस्पतिसमैरपि

mbh.3.183.30.m: Prosperity deludes a person, however wise and brave. Anyone living in comfort fails to notice it happening. That is my view.
mbh.3.183.30.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.30.sa: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् / वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम

mbh.3.183.33.m: Once I moved through the sky in a celestial chariot, drunk on pride, and gave no thought to anyone else.
mbh.3.183.33.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.33.sa: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानन चरन्पुरा / अभिमानेन मत्तः सन्कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्

mbh.3.183.43.m: Truth, self-control, discipline, steadiness, harmlessness and constant learning are what make a person good, O king, not birth or family.
mbh.3.183.43.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.43.sa: सत्यं दमस्तपो योगमहिंसा ज्ञाननित्यता / साधकानि सतां पुंसां न जातिर्नकुलं नृप

mbh.3.183.5.m: Sometimes truth outweighs giving, and sometimes giving outweighs truth. Likewise, harmlessness can matter more than pleasant speech. It depends on what the situation requires.
mbh.3.183.5.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.5.sa: क्वचिद्दानप्रयोगाद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते / सत्यवाक्याच्च राजेनद्र क्वचिद्दानं विशिष्यते

mbh.3.192.43.m: Seeing everything, moving and unmoving, lost in a single ocean, you were distressed. I knew it, and so I showed you the world.
roles: Shows God knowing the devotee's distress.
mbh.3.192.43.sa: सर्वमेकार्णवं दृष्ट्वा नष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम् / विक्लबोसि मया ज्ञातस्ततस्ते दर्शितं जगत्

scene.s: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
scene.t: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf

mbh.3.192.56.m: Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
mbh.3.192.56.sa: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः

mbh.3.210.44.m: Never give up what is right out of desire, rage or hatred. Don't be overjoyed by what pleases you, nor burn with distress at what does not.
roles: Holding to dharma under pull is shown.
mbh.3.210.44.sa: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्

mbh.3.210.46.m: Keep your mind on what is good and commit yourself to it. Do not become wicked in return for wickedness; always remain good.
mbh.3.210.46.sa: यत्कल्याणमभिध्यायेत्तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत् / न पापं प्रति पापः स्यात्साधुरेव सदा भवेत्

mbh.3.210.51.m: A fool does not shine in the world by praising himself; but a truly accomplished person shines even without polish.
mbh.3.210.51.sa: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया / अपिचेह मृजाहीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते

mbh.3.210.53.m: One who feels remorse for a wrong deed is freed from that wrong; by resolving 'I will not do it again', he is freed from the second.
roles: Shows the vow 'not again' is the second release.
mbh.3.210.53.sa: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते

mbh.3.210.59.m: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
roles: Shows turning to good clears the past.
mbh.3.210.59.sa: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः

mbh.3.211.34.m: Recalling the conduct of the good, the wise name just three steps: never betray anyone, give, and always speak the truth.
mbh.3.211.34.sa: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः सतां वृत्तमनुस्मरन् / न चैव द्रुह्येद्दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्

mbh.3.211.8.m: The essence of the Veda is truth; the essence of truth is self-control; the essence of self-control is letting go. This is always the way of the good.

mbh.3.213.43.m: The person who is free of envy and grateful keeps to what is good, and finds happiness, right living, prosperity and heaven.
roles: Names gratitude as a source of well-being.
mbh.3.213.43.sa: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः

mbh.3.216.50.m: Do not harm any living being; move through life with friendliness. Having been given this life, do not make an enemy of anyone.
roles: Cultivates friendliness as the way of moving through life.
mbh.3.216.50.sa: न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत् / नेदं जीवितमासाद्यवैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्

mbh.3.262.51.m: After happiness comes sorrow, and after sorrow, happiness. They come round to a person in turn, like the spokes of a wheel to the rim.
mbh.3.262.51.sa: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम् / पर्यायेणोपसर्पन्ते नरं नेमिमरा इव

mbh.3.264.10.m: Most worthy, giver of boons, endless one, you who give a way to those who have no way; ancient Person, beyond the reach of breath, mind and thought.
roles: Shows turning to God as agati-gati.
mbh.3.264.10.sa: वरेण्य वरदानन्त अगतीनां गतिप्रद / पुराणपुरुष प्राणमनोवृत्त्याद्यगोचर

scene.s: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.
scene.t: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens

mbh.3.264.11.m: Overseer of all, highest overseer, I have come to you for refuge. Protect me in your kindness, O God, you who love those who come for refuge.
mbh.3.264.11.sa: सर्वाध्यक्ष पराध्यक्ष त्वामहं शरणं गता / पाहि मां कृपया देव शरणागतवत्सल

scene.s: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.
scene.t: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens

mbh.3.264.40.m: Knowing your danger from that very wrathful sage, and because Draupadi thought of me, sons of Pritha, I came quickly.
roles: Shows being remembered by the devotee moves him.
mbh.3.264.40.sa: भवतामापदं ज्ञात्वा ऋषेः परमकोपनात् / द्रौपद्या चिन्तितः पार्था अहं सत्वरमागतः

scene.s: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.
scene.t: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens

mbh.3.264.44.m: With you as our protector, Govinda, lord, we have crossed this impassable danger, like the drowning who reach a boat in the great ocean.
mbh.3.264.44.sa: त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द दुस्तरामापदं विभो / तीर्णाः प्लवमिवासाद्य मज्जमाना महार्णवे

scene.s: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.
scene.t: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens

mbh.3.264.8.m: Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed son of Devaki, imperishable one, Vasudeva, lord of the world, you who destroy the pain of those who bow to you.
roles: Shows prayer as the first movement in crisis.
mbh.3.264.8.sa: कृष्णकृष्ण महाबाहो देवकीनन्दनाव्यय / वासुदेव जगन्नाथ प्रणतार्तिविनाशन

scene.s: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.
scene.t: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens

mbh.3.28.27.m: If someone who once helped you later wrongs you, even badly, forgive that wrong in light of the help they gave.
mbh.3.28.27.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Old help is not erased by a later wrong.
mbh.3.28.27.sa: पूर्वोपकारी यस्ते स्यादपराधे गरीयसि / उपकारेण तत्तस्य क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनः

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
scene.t: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira

mbh.3.28.28.m: Those who did wrong out of foolishness should be forgiven, for good judgement is not easy for everyone to come by.
mbh.3.28.28.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.28.28.sa: अबुद्धिमाश्रितानां तु क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनाम् / न हि सर्वत्र पाण्डित्वं सुलभं पुरुषेण वै

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
scene.t: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira

mbh.3.28.6.m: Force is not always best, and forgiveness is not always best. Know this for certain, my child: both have their place.
mbh.3.28.6.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Shows firmness is given equal standing with forgiveness.
mbh.3.28.6.sa: न श्रेयः सततं तेजो न नित्यं श्रेयसी क्षमा / इति तात विजानीहि द्वयमेतदसंशयम्

mbh.3.29.12.m: One who does not get angry back at an angry person saves both himself and the other from great danger. He becomes the healer of both.
mbh.3.29.12.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Names the calm one called the physician of both.
mbh.3.29.12.sa: आत्मानं च परांश्चैव त्रायते महतो भयात् / क्रुध्यन्तमप्रतिक्रुध्यन्दूयोरेष चिकित्सकः

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
scene.t: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira

mbh.3.29.20.m: The person who checks anger the moment it rises, using wisdom, is the one the wise call truly powerful.
mbh.3.29.20.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Redefines power as mastery of anger.
mbh.3.29.20.sa: वस्तु क्रोधं समुत्पन्नं प्रज्ञया परिबाधते / तेजस्विनं तं विदुषो मन्यन्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
scene.t: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira

mbh.3.29.28.m: If there were no people among us as patient as the earth, there would be no reconciliation between human beings, for every quarrel has its root in anger.
mbh.3.29.28.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.28.sa: यदि न स्युर्मानुषेषु क्षमिणः पृथिवीसमाः / न स्यात्सन्धिर्मनुष्याणां क्रोधमूलो हि विग्रहः

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
scene.t: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira

mbh.3.29.40.m: Forgiveness is the sacred; forgiveness is truth; forgiveness is what was and what will be. Forgiveness is discipline and purity. It is forgiveness that holds this world together.
mbh.3.29.40.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Shows forbearance praised as the ground of everything.
mbh.3.29.40.sa: क्षमा ब्रह्म क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा भूतं च भावि च / क्षमा तपः क्षमा शौचं क्षमयेदं धृतं जगत्

scene.s: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
scene.t: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira

mbh.3.29.8.m: An angry person never knows what should be said and what should not. For the angry there is nothing they won't do, and nothing they won't say.
mbh.3.29.8.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Pictures the angry mind for which nothing is off limits.
mbh.3.29.8.sa: वाच्यावाच्ये हि कुपितो न प्रजानाति कर्हिचित् / नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते तथा

mbh.3.297.7.m: Don't be distressed, father. I will see this vow through. It was begun with determination, and determination is what carries it to the end.
mbh.3.297.7.sa: न कार्यस्तात संतापः पारयिष्याम्यहं व्रतम् / व्यसंसायकृतं हीदं व्यवसायश्च कारणम्

mbh.3.298.24.m: The wise, who see what is true, say that walking seven steps together makes people friends. On the strength of that friendship, let me say something; please listen.
roles: Shows friendship forming quickly between those who walk together.
mbh.3.298.24.sa: प्राहुः साप्तपदं मैत्रं बुधास्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः / मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु

scene.s: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.
scene.t: Savitri and Satyavan

mbh.3.298.31.m: Even one meeting with good people is something to wish for; friendship with them is better still. Time with a good person is never wasted, so live among the good.
roles: Shows friendship with the good is called the higher gain.
mbh.3.298.31.sa: सतां सकृत्संगतमीप्सितं परं / ततः परं मित्रमिति प्रचक्षते / न चाफलं सत्पुरुषेण संगतं / ततः सतां संनिवसेत्समागमे

mbh.3.298.36.m: To bear no ill will toward any being in deed, thought or word, to help, and to give: this is the timeless way of the good.
mbh.3.298.36.sa: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः

mbh.3.298.44.m: Trust is born from goodwill toward all beings. That is why people place their trust above all in the good.
roles: Shows goodwill as the root of being trusted.
mbh.3.298.44.sa: सौहदात्सर्वभूतानां विश्वासो नाम जायते / तस्मात्सत्सु विशेपेण विश्वासं कुरुते जनः

mbh.3.298.50.m: Knowing this to be the noble, timeless way, the good keep working for others' sake without looking for anything in return.
mbh.3.298.50.sa: आर्यजुष्टमिदं वृत्तमिति विज्ञाय शाश्वतम् / सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ति प्रतिक्रियाः

mbh.3.31.2.m: I do not act rightly hungry for its reward, princess. I give because it ought to be given; I do what ought to be done.
mbh.3.31.2.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Shows a householder doing their part to the best of their ability.
mbh.3.31.2.sa: नाहं धर्मफलाकाङ्क्षी राजपुत्रि चराम्भुत / ददामि देयमित्येव यजे यष्टव्यमित्युत अस्तु वाऽत्र फलं मा वा कर्तव्यं पुरुषेण यत् / गृहे निवसता कृष्णे यथाशक्ति करोमि तत्

scene.s: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
scene.t: Do right without reward, and keep working

mbh.3.314.112.m: Readers, teachers and all others who merely mull over scripture are addicts and fools; the one who acts on it is the truly learned one.
mbh.3.314.112.sa: पठकाः पाठकाश्चैव ये चान्ये शास्त्रचिन्तकाः / सर्वे व्यसनिनो मूर्खा यः क्रियावान्स पण्डितः

mbh.3.314.114.m: Yaksha: 'What does one gain by speaking kindly? By acting after careful thought? By making many friends? By devotion to what is right?' Yudhishthira: 'One who speaks kindly is loved; one who acts after careful thought wins more; one with many friends lives happily; one devoted to what is right reaches the goal.'
roles: Shows kind speech and friendship linked to being loved and at ease.
mbh.3.314.114.sa: प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते / विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते / बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते / धर्मे रतः किं लभते कथय प्रियवचनवादी प्रीयो भवति / विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति / बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसत / यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते

mbh.3.314.116.m: Yaksha: 'Who is happy? What is the wonder? What is the path? What is the news?' Yudhishthira (on the wonder): 'Day after day, living beings go to the house of Death, yet those who remain want to stay forever. What could be more wondrous than that?'
mbh.3.314.116.sa: कोमोदतेकिमाश्चर्यं कः पन्थाः का च वार्तिका / वद मे चतुरः प्रश्नान्मृता जीवन्तु बान्धवाः अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम् / शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्

mbh.3.314.119.m: Reasoning has no firm footing; the scriptures disagree; there is no single sage whose word settles it. The truth of dharma is hidden in a cave. The path is the one the great have walked.
roles: Shows trust in lived example over endless debate.
mbh.3.314.119.sa: तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना / नैको मुनिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् / धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां / महाजनो येन गतःस पन्था

mbh.3.314.120.m: With the earth as the pot and the sky as its lid, with the sun as the fire and days and nights as the fuel, stirring with the ladle of months and seasons, Time is cooking all beings: that is the news.
roles: Shows all beings in the same pot.
mbh.3.314.120.sa: पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिघानं / सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन / मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन / भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता

mbh.3.314.121.m: Yaksha: 'You have answered my questions truly. Now tell me who is truly a person, and who possesses every wealth.' Yudhishthira: 'One to whom the pleasant and the unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future are all alike: he is called a true person.'
roles: Names evenness as the mark of the full person.
mbh.3.314.121.sa: व्याख्याता मे त्वया प्रश्ना यथातत्वं परंतप / पुरुषं त्विदानींव्याख्याहि यश्च सर्वधनी नरः तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये यस् सुखदुःखे तथैव च / अतीतानागते चोभे सवै पुरुष उच्येत

mbh.3.314.132.m: Kindness is the highest dharma, higher in my view than even the highest gain. I want to act with kindness: let Nakula live, Yaksha.
mbh.3.314.132.sa: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्चमे मतम् / आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु

scene.s: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
scene.t: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake

mbh.3.314.61.m: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
roles: Shows mother and father ranked above earth and sky.
mbh.3.314.61.sa: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्

mbh.3.314.65.m: Yaksha: 'Who is the friend of one away from home? Who is the friend of one at home? Who is the friend of the sick? Who is the friend of one about to die?' Yudhishthira: 'Learning is the friend of one abroad; a spouse is the friend at home; the doctor is the friend of the sick; what one has given is the friend of the dying.'
roles: Names who actually stands by one in each state.
mbh.3.314.65.sa: किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस् च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस्य भिषङ्भित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः

mbh.3.314.71.m: Yaksha: 'What single step leads to righteousness? What single step to good name? What single step to heaven? What single step to happiness?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the one step to righteousness; giving, to good name; truth, to heaven; good character, to happiness.'
mbh.3.314.71.sa: किंस्विदेकपदं धर्म्यं किंस्विदेकपदं यशः / किंस्विदेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं किंस्विदेकपदं सुखम् दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः / सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदंसुखम्

mbh.3.314.75.m: Yaksha: 'What is the best of good fortunes? The best of riches? The best of gains? The best of joys?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the best fortune; learning is the best wealth; health is the best gain; contentment is the highest happiness.'
roles: Shows health counted as the best gain.
mbh.3.314.75.sa: धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् / लाभानामुत्तमं किंस्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमं धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यंधनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् / लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा

mbh.3.314.89.m: Yaksha: 'What is called austerity? What is self-restraint? What is the highest forbearance? What is shame?' Yudhishthira: 'Austerity is staying true to one's own duty; restraint is taming the mind; forbearance is bearing life's opposites; shame is turning back from what should not be done.'
roles: Shows bearing heat and cold, gain and loss.
mbh.3.314.89.sa: तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः / क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वंहीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्

mbh.3.314.91.m: Yaksha: 'What is called knowledge? What is calm? What is the highest compassion? What is straightforwardness?' Yudhishthira: 'Knowledge is understanding things as they truly are; calm is a quiet mind; compassion is wishing happiness for all; straightforwardness is an even mind.'
mbh.3.314.91.sa: किं ज्ञानं प्रोच्यते राजन्कः शमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / दया च का परा प्रोक्ता किं चार्जवमुदाहृतम् ज्ञानं तत्त्वार्थसम्बोधः शमश्चित्तप्रशान्तता / दयासर्वसुखैपित्वमार्जवं समचित्तता

mbh.3.314.93.m: Yaksha: 'Which enemy is hardest to conquer? Which disease has no end? Who is considered good, and who is not?' Yudhishthira: 'Anger is the enemy hardest to conquer; greed is the disease without end; one who wants the good of all beings is good; one without compassion is not.'
roles: Names the good by goodwill to all beings.
mbh.3.314.93.sa: कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्चव्याधिरनन्तकः / कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभोव्याधिरनन्तकः / सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः

mbh.3.314.97.m: Yaksha: 'What do the sages call steadiness? What is fortitude? What is the best bath? What is true giving?' Yudhishthira: 'Steadiness is standing firm in one's duty; fortitude is mastery of the senses; the best bath is washing away the mind's impurities; true giving is protecting living beings.'
mbh.3.314.97.sa: किं स्थैर्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम् / स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्यं धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः / स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम्

mbh.3.32.14.m: The fool who just waits on fate, doing nothing and sleeping comfortably, sinks like an unbaked clay pot in water.
mbh.3.32.14.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Shows Draupadi insisting a person must act.
mbh.3.32.14.sa: यो हि दिष्टमुपासीत निर्विचेष्टः सुखं स्वपन् / अवसीदेत्सुदुर्बुद्धिरामो घट इवोदके

mbh.3.32.48.m: If the rain does not favour him, the farmer is not to blame. He tells himself: 'Whatever anyone could have done, I have done.' If the result is still this, the fault is not mine. Seeing this, the wise do not condemn themselves.
mbh.3.32.48.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Having done one's part is the ground to stand on.
mbh.3.32.48.sa: वृष्टिश्चेन्नानुगृह्णीयादनेनास्तत्र कर्षकः / यदन्यः पुरुषः कुर्यात्तत्कृतं सफलं मया तच्चेदं फलमस्माकमपराधो न मे क्वचित् / इति धीरोऽन्ववेक्ष्यैव नात्मानं तत्रगर्हयेत्

mbh.3.32.50.m: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
mbh.3.32.50.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Keeps the worker at the work.
mbh.3.32.50.sa: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः

mbh.3.32.58.m: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
mbh.3.32.58.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
roles: Names self-respect as the root of flourishing.
mbh.3.32.58.sa: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना

mbh.3.57.15.m: The more the king kept losing to Pushkara, the more his passion for the dice grew.
mbh.3.57.15.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
mbh.3.57.15.sa: यथायथा हि नृपतिः पुष्करेणैव जीयते / तथातथाऽस्य वै द्यूते रागो भूयोऽभिवर्धते

scene.s: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.
scene.t: Nala and Damayanti

mbh.5.129.11.m: You are the one most to blame here, Dhritarashtra, so fond of your son: you know his wrongdoing and still follow his lead.
mbh.5.129.11.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Shows love for a child does not excuse going along with wrong.
mbh.5.129.11.sa: त्वं ह्येवात्र भृशं गर्ह्यो धृतराष्ट्र सुतप्रियः / यो जानन्पापतामस्य तत्प्रज्ञामनुवर्तसे

scene.s: Summoned to the court, Queen Gandhari first blames her husband for indulging their son, then tells Duryodhana that whoever cannot rule himself cannot rule a kingdom, and that half the earth is enough.
scene.t: Gandhari counsels her son

mbh.5.129.27.m: Untamed senses are enough to destroy a person, the way unbroken horses can kill a poor charioteer on the road.
mbh.5.129.27.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.27.sa: अविधेयानि हीमानि व्यापादयितुमप्यलम् / अविधेया इवादान्ता हयाः पथि कुसारथिम्

mbh.5.129.29.m: First take your own self in hand, as you would an opponent. Then you won't fail to win over your advisers and your rivals.
mbh.5.129.29.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.29.sa: आत्मानमेव प्रथमं द्वेष्यरूपेण योजयेत् / ततोऽमात्यानमित्रांश्च न मोघं विजिगीषते

mbh.5.129.44.m: Half the earth is enough for you and your counsellors to live on. Listen to those who wish you well, and you will win a good name.
mbh.5.129.44.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.44.sa: अलमर्धं पृथिव्यास्ते महामात्यस्य जीवितुम् / सुहृदां वचने तिष्ठन्यशः प्राप्स्यति भारत

scene.s: Summoned to the court, Queen Gandhari first blames her husband for indulging their son, then tells Duryodhana that whoever cannot rule himself cannot rule a kingdom, and that half the earth is enough.
scene.t: Gandhari counsels her son

mbh.5.129.54.m: No one in this world gains real wealth through greed. Enough of greed, my son. Be at peace.
mbh.5.129.54.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.54.sa: न लोभादर्थसंपत्तिर्नराणामिह दृश्यते / तदलं तात लोभेन प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ ॥

mbh.5.133.14.m: Like a torch of tinduka wood, blaze, even if only for a moment. Do not smoulder without flame like a fire of husks, just to stay alive.
roles: Names a life with flame in it.
mbh.5.133.14.sa: अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि हि ज्वल / मा तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायस्व जिजीविषुः

scene.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
scene.t: Vidula rouses her defeated son

mbh.5.133.17.m: Whether he wins or fails, the wise person does not keep grieving. He starts on the next task at once and does not hoard his own life.
roles: Shows gain and failure getting the same response.
mbh.5.133.17.sa: अलब्ध्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः / आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते

mbh.5.133.21.m: Lift the load and pull it forward, remembering how a thoroughbred works. Summon your strength and your self-respect; know the power that is in you.
roles: Names mana, self-respect, to be summoned.
mbh.5.133.21.sa: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकतं स्मरन् / कुरु सत्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः

scene.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
scene.t: Vidula rouses her defeated son

mbh.5.133.7.m: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
roles: Set the mind on what is truly good.
mbh.5.133.7.sa: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर

scene.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
scene.t: Vidula rouses her defeated son

mbh.5.135.25.m: Son, don't look down on yourself because of past failures. Fortunes that never were come to be, and fortunes that were are lost. But don't start things out of mere resentment, like a fool.
roles: Shows fortunes move so the present low is not final.
