mbh.5.135.25.sa: पुत्र नात्मावमन्तव्यः पूर्वाभिरसमृद्धिभिः / अभूत्वा हि भवन्त्यर्था भूत्वा नश्यन्ति चापरे / अमर्षेणैव चाप्यर्था नारब्धव्याः सुबालिशैः

mbh.5.135.26.m: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
mbh.5.135.26.sa: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्

mbh.5.136.1.m: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
mbh.5.136.1.sa: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्

scene.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
scene.t: Vidula rouses her defeated son

mbh.5.27.26.m: Even if you win this whole earth to the edge of the sea, you will not escape old age and death, or the pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow.
mbh.5.27.26.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Sanjaya's counsel
roles: Shows conquest does not exempt anyone from the human lot.
mbh.5.27.26.sa: लब्ध्वाऽपीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां / जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः / प्रियाप्रिये सुखदुःखे च राज- / न्नैवं विद्वान्नैव युद्धं कुरु त्वम्

scene.s: Dhritarashtra's envoy Sanjaya begs Yudhishthira not to fight for a kingdom: life is short, and no conquest saves anyone from age, loss or death.
scene.t: Sanjaya's plea for peace

mbh.5.33.106.m: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, a good upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, speaking little, giving as much as one can, and gratitude.
mbh.5.33.106.sa: अष्टौ गुमाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति / प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च / पराक्रमश्चाबहुभाषिता च / दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च

mbh.5.33.108.m: Ten people do not know what is right, Dhritarashtra; hear who they are: the drunk, the careless, the deranged, the exhausted, the angry, the starving, the hurried, the greedy, the frightened and the lustful. So a wise person does not let himself be caught in these states.
roles: Check one's own state before judging what is right.
mbh.5.33.108.sa: दश धर्मं न जानन्ति धृतराष्ट्र निबोध तान् / मत्तः प्रमत्त उन्मत्तः श्रान्तः क्रुद्धो बुभुक्षितः त्वरमाणश्च लुब्धश्च भीतः कामी च ते दश / तस्मादेतेषु भावेषु न प्रसञ्जेत पण्डितः

mbh.5.33.119.m: He does not rekindle a quarrel that has died down, does not climb onto his pride, stays calm, and does not do wrong telling himself 'I am in a bad way': the noble call such conduct the best.
roles: Shows hard times not taken as licence.
mbh.5.33.119.sa: न वैरमुद्दिपयति प्रशान्तं / न दर्पमारोहति शान्तिमेति / न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोत्यकार्यं / तमार्यशीलं परमाहुरार्याः

mbh.5.33.120.m: He does not gloat over his own happiness, takes no pleasure in another's sorrow, and does not regret what he has given: such a person is called good and noble.
roles: Shows goodwill in both one's joy and another's pain.
mbh.5.33.120.sa: न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं / नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रहृष्टः / दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं / स कथ्यते सत्पुरुषार्यशीलः

mbh.5.33.14.m: Sleeplessness takes hold of a weak man attacked by a stronger one, of one without resources, of one who has lost his wealth, of the lustful, and of the thief.
roles: Shows a sleepless night as the subject.
mbh.5.33.14.sa: अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् / हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः

scene.s: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
scene.t: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool

mbh.5.33.29.m: He understands quickly, listens patiently, acts on understanding and not on impulse, and does not meddle in other people's affairs unasked: this is the first mark of a wise person.
roles: Names staying out of what one was not asked into.
mbh.5.33.29.sa: क्षिप्रं विजानाति चिरं श्रृणोति / विज्ञाय चार्यं भजते न कामात् / नासंपृष्टो व्युपयुङ्क्ते परार्थे / तत्प्रज्ञानं प्रथमं पण्डितस्य

mbh.5.33.30.m: The wise do not long for what cannot be had, do not choose to keep grieving over what is lost, and do not lose their heads in misfortune.
mbh.5.33.30.sa: नाप्राप्यमभिवाञ्छन्ति नष्टं नेच्छन्ति शोचितुम् / आपत्सु च न मुह्यन्ति नराः पण्डितबुद्धयः

mbh.5.33.31.m: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
mbh.5.33.31.sa: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते

mbh.5.33.33.m: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
mbh.5.33.33.sa: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते

mbh.5.33.42.m: He drags out what needs doing, doubts everything, and is slow where speed is needed: such a person is a fool, best of the Bharatas.
roles: Depicts stretching out what needs doing.
mbh.5.33.42.sa: संसारयति कृत्यानि सर्वत्र विचिकित्सते / चिरं करोति क्षिप्रार्थे स मूढो भरतर्षभ

mbh.5.33.45.m: One who blames another for a fault he himself has, and one who rages when he has no power to act, is the greatest of fools.
roles: Heals anger by showing powerless anger as self-harm.
mbh.5.33.45.sa: परं क्षिपति दोषेण वर्तमानः स्वयं तथा / यश्च क्रुध्यत्यनीशानः स च मूढतमो नरः

mbh.5.33.55.m: The forgiving have one fault and no second: people take a forgiving person to be weak. That should not be counted against him, for forgiveness is the greatest strength. In the weak it is a virtue; in the strong it is an ornament.
mbh.5.33.55.sa: एकः क्षमावतां दोषो द्वितीयो नोपपद्यते / यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः सोऽस्य दोषो न मन्तव्यः क्षमा हि परमं बलम् / क्षमा गुणो ह्यशक्तानां शक्तानां भूषणं क्षमा

mbh.5.33.85.m: Six faults must be given up by anyone who wants to prosper: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
roles: Shows clearing what stands in the way of rising.
mbh.5.33.85.sa: षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता / निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता

mbh.5.33.96.m: Health, freedom from debt, living at home, the company of good people, a livelihood of one's own, and living without fear: these, O king, are the six joys of this world.
roles: Shows letting a reader notice which of the six they already have.
mbh.5.33.96.sa: आरोग्यमानृण्यमविप्रवासः / सद्भिर्मनुष्यैः सह संप्रयोगः / स्वप्रत्यया वृत्तिरभीतवासः / षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन्

mbh.5.33.97.m: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the short-tempered, the ever-suspicious, and one who lives off another's fortune: these six are always unhappy.
roles: Cultivates contentment as the way out.
mbh.5.33.97.sa: ईर्षुर्धृणी नसन्तुष्टः क्रोधनो नित्यशङ्कितः / परभाग्योपजीवी च षडेते नित्यदुःखिताः

mbh.5.34.19.m: 'What will happen to me if I do this? What will happen if I don't?' Thinking actions through this way, a person should then act, or not act.
mbh.5.34.19.sa: किं नु मे स्यादिदं कृत्वा किं नु मे स्यादकुर्वतः / इति कर्माणि सञ्चिन्त्य कुर्याद्वा पुरुषो न वा

mbh.5.34.43.m: One who envies others their wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness, good fortune or honours suffers from a disease without end.
roles: Shows envy fixing on exactly what it lists.
mbh.5.34.43.sa: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः

mbh.5.34.7.m: And if a task undertaken with the right means and done with proper method still does not succeed, the wise person should not let his mind sink over it.
roles: Shows steadiness after a clean failure.
mbh.5.34.7.sa: तथैव योगविहितं यत्तु कर्म न सिध्यति / उपाययुक्तं मेधावी न तत्र ग्लपयेन्मनः

mbh.5.34.75.m: Fools wound the wise with abuse and slander. The one who speaks takes on the wrong; the one who bears it patiently is set free.
mbh.5.34.75.sa: आक्रोशपरिवादाभ्यां विहिंसन्त्यबुधा बुधान् / वक्ता पापमुपादत्ते क्षममाणो विमुच्यते

mbh.5.34.79.m: A forest pierced by arrows or felled by the axe grows back; but a wound made by cruel, ugly words does not heal.
roles: Shows the permanence of what a sentence does for the speaker.
mbh.5.34.79.sa: रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् / वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्

mbh.5.35.51.m: The gods do not guard a person with a stick in hand, the way a herdsman guards cattle. Whomever they wish to protect, they endow with good judgement.
mbh.5.35.51.sa: न देवा यष्टिमादाय रक्षन्ति पशुपालवत् / यं तु रक्षितुमिच्छन्ति बुद्ध्या संयोजयन्ति तम्

mbh.5.35.60.m: Gold is known by a flame of straw; a good person by conduct, an honest one by dealings, a brave one in danger, a steady one in money troubles, and friends and enemies in hard times.
roles: The steady one is known in want.
mbh.5.35.60.sa: तृणोल्कया ज्ञायते जातरूपं / वृत्तेन भद्रो व्यवहारेण साधुः / शूरो भयेष्वर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः / कृच्छ्रेष्वापत्सु सुहृदश्चारयश्च

mbh.5.35.61.m: Age steals beauty, craving steals patience, death takes life, envy takes goodness, anger takes prosperity, bad company takes character, lust takes shame, and pride takes everything.
roles: Names pride as the thief of everything.
mbh.5.35.61.sa: जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा / मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया / क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्यसेवा / ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः

mbh.5.35.79.m: Do during the day what lets you sleep in peace at night; do in the eight dry months what lets you live comfortably through the rains. Do in youth what makes old age comfortable, and do all your life what brings peace after death.
roles: Shows choosing today's act by how it will sit at night.
mbh.5.35.79.sa: दिवसेनैव तत्कुर्याद्येन रात्रौ सुखं वसेत् / अष्टमासेन तत्कुर्याद्येन वर्षाः सुखं वसेत् पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धः सुखं वसेत् / यावज्जीवं तु तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत्

mbh.5.36.37.m: That is no friend whose anger you fear, or whom you must approach warily. A friend is one you can trust as you trust a father; the rest are mere acquaintances.
mbh.5.36.37.sa: न तन्मित्रं यस्य कोपाद्बिभेति / यद्वा मित्रं शङ्कितेनोपचर्यम् / यस्मिन्मित्रे पितरीवाश्वसीत / तद्वै मित्रं सङ्गतानीतराणि

mbh.5.36.44.m: Brooding destroys beauty, brooding destroys strength, brooding destroys understanding, brooding brings on illness. Grief does not get you what you want; it only wears out the body and gladdens your enemies. Do not give your mind to grief.
roles: Counts what brooding takes: strength, judgement, health.
mbh.5.36.44.sa: सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् / सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते / अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः

mbh.5.36.5.m: When insulted, do not insult back. The anger held in by one who forbears burns up the one who insulted him, and the forbearer gains his merit.
mbh.5.36.5.sa: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः / आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति

mbh.5.36.50.m: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
roles: Peace is said to come only by these means.
mbh.5.36.50.sa: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ

mbh.5.36.62.m: A single tree, however great, strong and deep-rooted, can be wrenched out trunk and all by the wind in a moment. But trees that stand together, rooted in a cluster, withstand the fiercest winds by leaning on one another.
roles: Shows mutual support among one's people.
mbh.5.36.62.sa: महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः / प्रसह्य एव वातेन सस्कन्धो मर्दितुं क्षणात् अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः / ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेन्योन्यसंश्रयात्

mbh.5.36.68.m: It is bitter without being a medicine, it gives you a headache, it leads to wrongdoing; it is harsh, sharp and hot. The good drink it down; the bad cannot. That is anger. Drink it, great king, and be at peace.
roles: Shows swallowing it is the mark of the good.
mbh.5.36.68.sa: अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्षरोगि / पापानुबन्धं परुषं तीक्ष्णमुष्णम् / सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो / मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य

scene.s: Vidura retells the sage Atreya's answer to the gods: don't insult back, hold your tongue, choose your company. He adds that anger is a bitter drink and that kin who stand together survive storms.
scene.t: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger

mbh.5.37.10.m: Excessive pride, talking too much, refusing to give, anger, selfishness and betraying friends: these six are sharp swords that cut short a person's life. It is these that kill people, not death.
mbh.5.37.10.sa: अतिमानोऽतिवादश्च तथाऽत्यागो नराधिप / क्रोधश्चात्मविधित्सा च मित्रद्रोहश्च तानि षट् एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् / एतानि मानवान्ध्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते

mbh.5.37.46.m: There is no forest without tigers, and no tigers without the forest. The tigers protect the forest, and the forest shelters the tigers.
mbh.5.37.46.sa: न स्याद्वनमृते व्याघ्रान्व्याघ्रा न स्युर्ऋते वनम् / वनं हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैर्व्याघ्रान्रक्षति काननम्

scene.s: Vidura lists Manu's seventeen kinds of fool and the six habits, from arrogance to betraying friends, that shorten a life more surely than death. He warns that the cousins need each other like a forest and its tigers.
scene.t: Vidura Niti: what cuts life short

mbh.5.37.51.m: Whoever reins in the rush of anger and of elation the moment they rise, and does not lose his head in trouble, is the one good fortune favours.
mbh.5.37.51.sa: सन्नियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः / स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति

mbh.5.38.16.m: Don't talk about what you are going to do; let people see only what you have done. That way your plans for duty, pleasure and gain are never exposed.
mbh.5.38.16.sa: करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव तु दर्शयेत् / धर्मकामार्थकार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते

mbh.5.39.2.m: Even Brihaspati, if he speaks before the right time, earns contempt for his wisdom and is disrespected.
roles: Shows choose the moment to speak.
mbh.5.39.2.sa: अप्राप्तकालं वचनं बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन् / लभते बुध्द्यवज्ञानमवमानं च भारत

mbh.5.39.51.m: Everyone wants as a friend someone grateful, principled, truthful, big-hearted, loyal, self-controlled and steady.
mbh.5.39.51.sa: कृतज्ञं धार्मिकं सत्यमक्षुद्रं दृढभक्तिकम् / जितेन्द्रियं स्थितं स्थित्यां मित्रमित्यभिवाञ्छति

mbh.5.39.56.m: Whatever a person keeps doing, in action, thought or word, is what carries him away. So keep doing what is good.
mbh.5.39.56.sa: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यदभीक्ष्णं निषेवते / तदेवापहरत्येनं तस्मात्कल्याणमाचरेत्

mbh.5.39.6.m: A gain that brings loss should not be valued; a loss that brings gain should be valued.
mbh.5.39.6.sa: न वृद्धिर्बहुमन्तव्या या वृद्धिः क्षयमावहेत् / क्षयोऽपि बहुमन्तव्यो यः क्षयो वृद्धिमावहेत्

mbh.5.39.63.m: A person who is straightforward, and modest because of it, is taken for weak by small-minded people, and they push him around.
mbh.5.39.63.sa: आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात्सव्यपत्रपम् / अशक्तं मन्यमानास्तु धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः

mbh.5.40.12.m: Here is the highest thing I can tell you, the purest and most valuable: never abandon what is right, not out of desire, not out of fear, not out of greed, not even to save your life.
roles: Holding to what is right at cost.
mbh.5.40.12.sa: इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि / पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् / न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभा- / द्धर्मं जह्याज्जीविस्यापि हेतोः

mbh.5.40.18.m: When a person is laid on the pyre, only the deeds he himself did go with him. So gather goodness carefully, a little at a time.
mbh.5.40.18.sa: अग्नौ प्रास्तं तु पुरुषं कर्मान्वेति स्वयं कृतम् / तस्मात्तु पुरुषो यत्नाद्धर्मं सञ्चिनुयाच्छनैः

mbh.5.40.22.m: Make steadiness your boat and cross the river whose water is the five senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger.
mbh.5.40.22.sa: कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम् / नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर

mbh.5.40.23.m: One who honours and wins over a kinsman mature in wisdom, in goodness, in learning and in years, and asks him what should and should not be done, is never confused.
mbh.5.40.23.sa: प्रज्ञावृद्धं धर्मवृद्धं स्वबन्धुं / विद्यावृद्धं वयसा चापि वृद्धम् / कार्याकार्ये पूजयित्वा प्रसाद्य / यः संपृच्छेन्न स मुह्येत्कदाचित्

mbh.5.42.13.m: A person who runs after desires perishes along with them; one who sets desires aside shakes off whatever dust clings to him.
roles: Shows setting desires aside clears the dust.
mbh.5.42.13.sa: कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामाननु विनश्यति / कामान्व्युदस्य धुनुते यत्किञ्चित्पुरुषो रजः

mbh.5.42.35.m: One who is one thing but presents himself as another: what wrong has that thief not committed, who robs his own self?
roles: Shows knowing the self as it is.
mbh.5.42.35.sa: योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते / किं तेन न कृतं पापं चोरेणात्मापहारिणा

mbh.5.42.4.m: Both views are true, O king, and both have been held from the beginning. The wise regard delusion as death. I say that heedlessness is death, and heedfulness is immortality.
roles: Names Apramada, wakeful attention, as the deathless state.
mbh.5.42.4.sa: उभे सत्ये क्षत्रियाद्य प्रवृत्ते / मोहो मृत्युः संमतोऽयं कवीनाम् / प्रमादं वै मृत्युमहं ब्रवीमि / तथाऽप्रमादममृतत्वं ब्रवीमि

mbh.5.43.61.m: One does not become a sage by keeping silent, nor by living in the forest. One who knows his own true nature is called the best of sages.
roles: Shows sagehood knowing one's own nature.
mbh.5.43.61.sa: मौनान्न स मुनिर्भवति नारण्यवसनान्मुनिः / स्वलक्षणं तु यो वेद स मुनिः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते

mbh.5.71.26.m: When someone from a good family covets others' wealth, greed kills his judgement; lost judgement kills his sense of shame; lost shame wears away right conduct, and with it goes prosperity, and then the person himself.
mbh.5.71.26.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.26.sa: कुले जातस्य वृद्धस्य परवित्तेषु गृद्ध्यतः / लोभः प्रज्ञानमाहन्ति प्रज्ञा हन्ति हता ह्रियं ह्रीर्हता बाधते धर्मं धर्मो हन्ति हतः श्रियम् / श्रीर्हता पुरुषं हन्ति पुरुषस्याधं वधः

mbh.5.71.28.m: When a man has no money, relatives, friends and brahmins turn away from him, the way birds leave a tree that has no flowers and no fruit.
mbh.5.71.28.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Depicts feeling like the bare tree.
mbh.5.71.28.sa: अधनाद्धि निवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदो द्विजाः / अपुष्पादफलाद्वृक्षाद्यथा कृष्ण पतत्रिणः

mbh.5.71.37.m: Someone born poor does not suffer as much as someone who had good fortune, grew used to comfort, and then lost it.
mbh.5.71.37.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Shows a person fallen from a life one was used to.
mbh.5.71.37.sa: न तथा बाध्यते कृष्ण प्रकृत्या निर्धनो जनः / यथा भद्रां श्रियं प्राप्य तया हीनः सुखैधितः

mbh.5.71.38.m: Having fallen into great trouble through his own fault, he blames the gods, even Indra, but never himself.
mbh.5.71.38.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Shows looking at one's own part.
mbh.5.71.38.sa: स तदाऽऽत्मापराधेन संप्राप्तो व्यसनं महत् / सेन्द्रान्गर्हयते देवान्नात्मानं च कथंचन

mbh.5.71.67.m: Victory breeds hostility, and the defeated live in pain. The one at peace, who has set aside winning and losing, sleeps well.
mbh.5.71.67.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.67.sa: सर्वोच्छेदे च यतते वैरस्यान्तविधित्सया / जयो वैरं प्रसृजति दुःखमास्ते पराजितः सुखं प्रशान्तः स्वपिति हित्वा जयपराजयौ / जातवैरश्च पुरुषो दुःखं स्वपिति नित्यदा

scene.s: Before Krishna sets out as peace envoy, Yudhishthira opens his heart: poverty humiliates, greed corrodes, victory breeds enmity, and hostility is never ended by hostility. He asks only for five villages.
scene.t: Yudhishthira's case for peace

mbh.5.71.71.m: Hostility is never ended by hostility, Keshava. It only grows, like fire fed with ghee.
mbh.5.71.71.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Shows only a non-hostile response can close it.
mbh.5.71.71.sa: आख्यातारश्च विद्यन्ते पुमांश्चेद्विद्यते कुले / न चापि वैरं वैरेण केशव व्युपशाम्यति हविषाऽग्निर्यथा कृष्ण भूय एवाभिवर्धते / अतोऽन्यथा नास्ति शान्तिर्नित्यमन्तरमन्ततः

scene.s: Before Krishna sets out as peace envoy, Yudhishthira opens his heart: poverty humiliates, greed corrodes, victory breeds enmity, and hostility is never ended by hostility. He asks only for five villages.
scene.t: Yudhishthira's case for peace

mbh.5.71.92.m: No wealth would please us, nor godhood, let alone mere comfort, nor even lordship over all the gods, if it came by betraying you, Madhava.
mbh.5.71.92.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Shows loyalty placed above every gain.
mbh.5.71.92.sa: न हि नः प्रीणयेद्द्रव्यं न देवत्वं कुतः सुखम् / न च सर्वामरैश्वर्यं तव द्रोहेण माधव

mbh.5.81.26.m: While the sons of Pandu sat without anger or movement, only watching, I thought of you in my mind, Govinda: 'Protect me!'
roles: She says it aloud to Krishna and demands it be answered.
mbh.5.81.26.sa: निरमर्षेष्वचेष्टेषु प्रेक्ष्यमाणेषु पाण्डुषु / पाहि मामिति गोविन्द मनसा चिन्तितोसि मे

scene.s: Krishna visits the exiled Pandavas in the Kamyaka forest and tells Arjuna 'you are mine and I am yours'. Draupadi then comes to him 'seeking refuge with the refuge', tells him, out of closeness, everything done to her in the dice-hall and since, and weeps that she has no one, not even him. Krishna promises she will see justice.
scene.t: Draupadi tells Krishna her sorrow

mbh.5.95.46.m: We have treated you as a father; treat us the same way. When children go astray, it is the father's duty to set them back on the path.
mbh.5.95.46.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: Shows a respectful, direct claim on a parent's fairness.
mbh.5.95.46.sa: वर्तामहे त्वयि च तां त्वं च वर्तस्व नस्तथा / पित्रा स्थापयितव्या हि वयमुत्पथमास्थिताः

scene.s: Krishna travels to Hastinapura to plead for peace between the cousins. Elders, sages and finally Gandhari urge Duryodhana to share the kingdom; he refuses, even plotting to seize Krishna, and war becomes certain.
scene.t: Krishna's peace embassy to the Kauravas

mbh.5.95.48.m: Where right is struck down by wrong and truth by falsehood while the assembly looks on, it is the onlookers who are struck down.
mbh.5.95.48.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
roles: The text stands with the one wronged in public.
mbh.5.95.48.sa: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसांप्रतम् / यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः / विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते

st.mbh.ashtavakra_cursed_for_correcting_.l: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.
st.mbh.ashtavakra_cursed_for_correcting_.s: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.

st.mbh.ashtavakra_too_young_at_the_door.l: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.
st.mbh.ashtavakra_too_young_at_the_door.s: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.

st.mbh.bali_after_the_fall.l: Success is on loan. Don't gloat in a good season or despair in a bad one.
st.mbh.bali_after_the_fall.s: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his defeated rival Bali living as a donkey in an empty house and mocks him. Bali calmly answers that fortune has lived with a thousand Indras before, that time gives and takes, and that this is a season for calm.
st.mbh.bali_after_the_fall.t: Bali and Indra: the fortune that moves on

st.mbh.bhima_cannot_lift_the_tail.l: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.
st.mbh.bhima_cannot_lift_the_tail.s: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.

st.mbh.bhima_in_the_pythons_grip.l: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.
st.mbh.bhima_in_the_pythons_grip.s: A giant python seizes Bhima. It is King Nahusha, once lord of heaven, cursed for making sages carry his palanquin. He frees Bhima after Yudhishthira answers his questions on goodness, and is freed himself.
st.mbh.bhima_in_the_pythons_grip.t: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers

st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.l: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.l: At the end, it is enough to say: I am yours; now let me go.
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.s: When the sun turns north, Bhishma, after fifty-eight nights on the arrows, takes leave of the family, asks Krishna to protect him and to give him leave to go. Krishna says there is no fault in him and lets him go; Bhishma's last words to the family are to hold to truth and kindness.
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.t: Bhishma asks Krishna's leave to die

st.mbh.bhishma_pillow_of_arrows.l: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
st.mbh.bhishma_pillow_of_arrows.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
st.mbh.bhishma_pillow_of_arrows.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

st.mbh.cat_and_mouse_truce.l: Sometimes you must cooperate with a rival; do it with clear eyes.
st.mbh.cat_and_mouse_truce.s: Caught between a mongoose, an owl and a trapped cat, the mouse Palita makes a deal: he will gnaw the cat free if the cat protects him. Both keep the bargain, then part warily.

st.mbh.dharmavyadha_sends_him_home.l: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.
st.mbh.dharmavyadha_sends_him_home.s: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
st.mbh.dharmavyadha_sends_him_home.t: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_sleep.l: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_sleep.s: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_cannot_sleep.t: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool

st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back.l: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

st.mbh.five_villages.l: Winning a feud still costs you peace. Hostility only ends when someone stops feeding it.
st.mbh.five_villages.s: Before Krishna sets out as peace envoy, Yudhishthira opens his heart: poverty humiliates, greed corrodes, victory breeds enmity, and hostility is never ended by hostility. He asks only for five villages.

st.mbh.gautama_kills_his_benefactor.l: Gratitude is the root of every friendship. Betraying a benefactor poisons everything after.
st.mbh.gautama_kills_his_benefactor.s: A destitute brahmin, Gautama, is fed and sheltered by a kind crane, Rajadharma, and made rich by the crane's friend. On the way home he kills his sleeping benefactor for food. Bhishma ends: there is atonement for many wrongs, none for ingratitude.

st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.l: Words fly like arrows. The one who doesn't answer anger with anger stands highest.
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.s: Prajapati, in the form of a golden swan, answers the Sadhyas: never speak words that make others flinch, don't insult back, ride out the urges of speech and anger, and remember that we become our company.
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.t: Hamsa Gita: the swan's teaching on speech and anger

st.mbh.is_anyone_unluckier_than_me.l: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
st.mbh.is_anyone_unluckier_than_me.s: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

st.mbh.jajali_and_tuladhara.l: Goodness is everyday fairness and friendliness, not spiritual display.
st.mbh.jajali_and_tuladhara.s: The ascetic Jajali, proud because birds nest in his matted hair, is told to learn from a trader in Varanasi. Tuladhara teaches that right living is being a friend to all in thought, word and deed, and dealing fairly.
st.mbh.jajali_and_tuladhara.t: Tuladhara and Jajali: the merchant who taught the ascetic

st.mbh.janaka_and_his_queen.l: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.janaka_and_his_queen.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
st.mbh.janaka_and_his_queen.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

st.mbh.krishna_asks_bhishma_to_teach.l: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
st.mbh.krishna_asks_bhishma_to_teach.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
st.mbh.krishna_asks_bhishma_to_teach.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

st.mbh.krishna_family_troubles.l: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.
st.mbh.krishna_family_troubles.s: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
st.mbh.krishna_family_troubles.t: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron

st.mbh.krishna_goes_knowing_it_will_fail.l: You can make the best case for peace and still be refused. Speak anyway.
st.mbh.krishna_goes_knowing_it_will_fail.s: Krishna travels to Hastinapura to plead for peace between the cousins. Elders, sages and finally Gandhari urge Duryodhana to share the kingdom; he refuses, even plotting to seize Krishna, and war becomes certain.
st.mbh.krishna_goes_knowing_it_will_fail.t: Krishna's peace embassy to the Kauravas

st.mbh.manki_and_the_two_young_bulls.l: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
st.mbh.manki_and_the_two_young_bulls.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
st.mbh.manki_and_the_two_young_bulls.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root

st.mbh.markandeya_finds_the_child.l: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
st.mbh.markandeya_finds_the_child.s: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
st.mbh.markandeya_finds_the_child.t: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf

st.mbh.medhavin_wakes_his_father.l: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
st.mbh.medhavin_wakes_his_father.s: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
st.mbh.medhavin_wakes_his_father.t: Medhavin: the son who woke his father

st.mbh.nala_as_bahuka.l: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
st.mbh.nala_as_bahuka.s: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

st.mbh.narada_many_causes_of_karnas_deat.l: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.narada_many_causes_of_karnas_deat.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
st.mbh.narada_many_causes_of_karnas_deat.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel

st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.l: In a family's darkest hour, the women's cry is heard and the promise kept.
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.s: Abhimanyu's son is born dead, struck in the womb by Ashvatthama's weapon. Kunti, Subhadra and Uttara beg Krishna for help, reminding him of his promise. Krishna, on the strength of his own truthfulness, revives the child, who is named Parikshit.
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.t: The stillborn heir and Krishna's promise

st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.l: Loyalty means staying through the bad season, not only the good.
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.s: A hunter's poisoned arrow withers the tree where a parrot has always lived. The parrot refuses to leave it. Indra, moved by its loyalty, restores the tree.
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.t: The parrot who stayed with the withered tree

st.mbh.pingala_stops_waiting.l: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
st.mbh.pingala_stops_waiting.s: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
st.mbh.pingala_stops_waiting.t: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting

st.mbh.river_and_the_reeds.l: Bend with the flood and you stand again after it passes.
st.mbh.river_and_the_reeds.s: The Ocean asks the rivers why they uproot great trees but never the reeds. Ganga answers: the reed bends when the flood comes and stands again after; the rigid tree breaks.

st.mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness_is_death.l: Carelessness is the real death. Stay awake to your life and be who you are.
st.mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness_is_death.s: At Vidura's request the ancient sage Sanatsujata answers Dhritarashtra's fear of death. Death, he says, is heedlessness; desire drags us down; pretending to be what we are not is self-theft.
st.mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness_is_death.t: Sanatsujatiya: the sage on death and the self

st.mbh.senajit_and_the_logs_in_the_sea.l: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.
st.mbh.senajit_and_the_logs_in_the_sea.s: King Senajit is crushed by his son's death. A brahmin comforts him: everyone suffers, no sorrow lasts forever, effort beats idleness, and whatever we call 'mine' becomes a source of pain.
st.mbh.senajit_and_the_logs_in_the_sea.t: King Senajit and the brahmin's consolation

st.mbh.shibi_and_the_dove.l: When duties collide, weigh them honestly, and keep your word to those who trust you.
st.mbh.shibi_and_the_dove.s: A frightened dove flies to King Shibi for refuge; a hawk demands it back as its rightful food. Shibi offers the hawk anything else, finally his own flesh weighed against the dove, and climbs onto the scale himself. The birds reveal themselves as gods.

st.mbh.srinjaya_and_the_sixteen_kings.l: Everyone we love is mortal; you are not singled out. Grief can still be met with care.
st.mbh.srinjaya_and_the_sixteen_kings.s: Krishna tells Yudhishthira how Narada consoled King Srinjaya, whose son had died, by recounting sixteen legendary kings far greater than his son who also died. Moved, Srinjaya listens, and Narada restores the boy.
st.mbh.srinjaya_and_the_sixteen_kings.t: The sixteen kings: Narada consoles Srinjaya

st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.l: A small gift, honestly earned and given from little, outweighs the grandest show.
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.s: At the end of Yudhishthira's lavish horse sacrifice, a half-golden mongoose declares it worth less than a poor family's gift. In a famine, a gleaner, his wife, son and daughter-in-law each gave their last handful of flour to a hungry guest; rolling in the spilt flour turned half the mongoose to gold.
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.t: The golden mongoose and the handful of flour

st.mbh.the_python_sage.l: Take what comes gladly; stop chasing what's out of reach.
st.mbh.the_python_sage.s: Prahlada meets a sage who lives like a python, taking what comes and not chasing. The sage explains how ceasing to chase made him content.

st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.l: The hardest battle is with your own mind, and no one else can fight it for you.
st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.s: As Yudhishthira still grieves, Krishna tells him his real battle has begun: one fought alone, with his own mind, where 'mine' is death and 'not mine' is freedom.

st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.l: You can try your best for peace and still fail. Others' choices are not your guilt.
st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.s: Returning home after the war, Krishna meets the sage Uttanka, who is furious that Krishna let the cousins destroy each other and threatens to curse him. Krishna explains that he tried hard for peace and was refused, and calms him.

st.mbh.vidula_rouses_her_son.l: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
st.mbh.vidula_rouses_her_son.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_ashamed_before_bhish.l: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_ashamed_before_bhish.s: After the war, Krishna sits motionless; he explains that the dying Bhishma is thinking of him, so his mind has gone to Bhishma. They visit; Bhishma sings his hymn to Krishna, admits his pain and that he stands only on Krishna's strength. Krishna grants him relief, asks the next morning whether he slept well, and steps back so that Bhishma, not he, will teach Yudhishthira.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_ashamed_before_bhish.t: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows

st.mbh.yudhishthira_at_the_lake.l: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_at_the_lake.s: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_at_the_lake.t: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake

st.mbh.yudhishthira_chooses_nakula.t: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake

st.mbh.yudhishthira_dharma_not_a_trade.l: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_dharma_not_a_trade.s: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_dharma_not_a_trade.t: Do right without reward, and keep working

st.mbh.yudhishthira_victory_like_defeat.l: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_victory_like_defeat.s: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_victory_like_defeat.t: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
